variants.title: Unreadable privacy policy allows mutations but discards their results
variants.detail: When loadOutputPrivacy returns null, the handler executes the tool before replacing its result with a generic message. It also returns success rather than an MCP error. For limitless_create_run this queues work but hides the generated run ID, preventing the caller from following the run or reliably determining whether a retry would duplicate it. Review and land similarly lose their mutation receipts.

variants.title: Privacy-policy failure now hides results of every existing MCP tool, including mutations
variants.detail: Every tool output now goes through loadOutputPrivacy(). If private-strings.txt cannot be read, every tool except status returns only {message: 'Tool output withheld; privacy policy unavailable.'}. That includes create_run, cancel_run, answer_question, review and land, which still carry out the mutation. The caller loses the created run id or the land entry and cannot tell whether the call worked, which invites a duplicate retry. Before this change these existing tools returned their results.

variants.title: If the privacy policy can't be read, tools that change state still act but hide their result
variants.detail: The CallTool handler now runs every tool and then, if `loadOutputPrivacy()` returned null, replaces the output of every tool except `limitless_status` with "Tool output withheld". So `limitless_create_run`, `limitless_land`, `limitless_review`, `limitless_answer_question` and `limitless_cancel_run` still make their change, but the agent gets no run id, land entry or approval back. The tool descriptions tell agents not to retry without inspecting state, but without the id they can't inspect it. This MCP-wide privacy layer, and the matching `\uXXXX` decoding added to the publication gate in src/gates/private.ts, were not asked for.

variants.title: limitless_status returns no state or nextAction when the privacy policy is unavailable
variants.detail: In the no-privacy branch, result() returns only {land:{id,state}, openQuestions} and drops `state` and `nextAction`, which are the tool's whole purpose. Both strings are hard-coded enum-like text, apart from the `round.runId` and `land.state` parts that are interpolated into them. The tool description does not mention this degraded shape.

variants.title: limitless_status drops its state and next action when the privacy policy can't be read
variants.detail: With no privacy policy, `result()` returns only `{land:{id,state}, openQuestions}`. The `state` and `nextAction` strings are fixed text written in this file and contain no untrusted data, yet they are dropped. The request says status returns a plain-language state and the next action.

variants.title: limitless_status drops its plain-language state and next action when the privacy policy is unavailable
variants.detail: When privacy is null, `result()` returns only `{land:{id,state}, openQuestions}`. The `state` and `nextAction` fields are left out, but those are the outputs the request asks for. Almost all of their text is constant and generated by the code. The only interpolated values are run IDs and the land-state enum.

variants.title: Digest quoting does not escape bidi or zero-width characters in untrusted PR titles
variants.detail: quote() uses JSON.stringify and also escapes U+007F–U+009F and U+2028/2029. Bidi overrides (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) and zero-width characters pass through unchanged. A PR title can visually reorder or hide parts of the quoted line in the terminal and in the SessionStart context, which weakens the 'quoted untrusted text' guarantee.

variants.title: Approved PRs with no saved PR snapshot are listed as awaiting review
variants.detail: The check `approval.sha !== pr?.headRefOid` is true whenever prSnapshot is missing, so a PR with a valid, non-stale approval and no saved observation is counted under 'PRs awaiting review'. limitless_status reports the same PR as 'PR state unknown', so the two outputs disagree.

variants.title: Unrequested change to the private-string gate decoder, and the change exceeds the ~200-line budget
variants.detail: The publication gate now decodes `\uXXXX` escapes in every scanned text, not only in the new MCP and digest output. This is stricter, so false positives become more likely in code that contains literal Unicode escapes. It falls outside the requested scope. Together with the new privacy layer applied to every MCP tool, source changes total about 450 lines against a budget of about 200.

variants.title: Unrequested change to the publication-gate decoder, and the diff is well over budget
variants.detail: The request set a budget of about 200 source lines and said to build on the existing APIs. The diff changes about 450 source lines. It adds a new privacy layer for all MCP outputs, approvedAt/createdAt plumbing in getRunDetail, and a change to `decoded()` in the publication private-strings gate, which now also decodes `\uXXXX` escapes. That gate change affects push and publication blocking for every run, not just the new MCP and digest output, and only the gates tests cover it.

variants.title: Publication-gate decoding changed outside the requested scope
variants.detail: privateMatches now also decodes literal \uXXXX escapes. That function is the shared publication gate used by the engine, not only the new output privacy. The change alters gate behaviour for all runs, which may block content that previously passed. Combined with the new private-output layer applied to every existing MCP tool, the diff goes well beyond the ~200-line budget and the stated feature.

variants.title: Digest lists PRs as awaiting review while their run is still in progress
variants.detail: The 'PRs awaiting review' filter checks only that the run is not resolved, cancelled or merged, that a PR exists, that the PR is not closed, and the approval and land state. It does not require the run to be finished. submitReview refuses any owner whose status is not succeeded or needs_human. So a run that opened its PR and is still running (CI wait, verify) shows up as review-ready, and a review verdict would be refused with 409. explainStatus handles this case as 'Work pending', so the two tools disagree.

variants.title: GET /api/land?run=<unknown> returns 400 rather than 404
variants.detail: LandQueue.list(runId) throws a plain Error('run not found'). The HTTP handle wrapper maps any thrown error to 400, so an unknown run is reported as a bad request instead of not found.

variants.title: Codex skill tells Codex to use the Claude consumer name
variants.detail: The Codex skill is a copy of the Claude skill and says `limitless digest --consumer claude`. Following it, a Codex session would read the cursor of the Claude consumer, and might acknowledge on it, instead of using its own consumer.

variants.title: Codex skill tells agents to run digest with --consumer claude
variants.detail: The Codex skill is a byte-for-byte copy of the Claude skill. It tells Codex sessions to run `limitless digest --consumer claude`, so Codex would read the Claude consumer's cursor rather than its own.

variants.title: Review and land return the backend result without schema validation
variants.detail: Every other tool checks the backend response against a zod schema before returning it, so a malformed response becomes a 'Malformed backend response' error. `limitless_review` and `limitless_land` return the raw `unknown` instead. Separately, the new server `instructions` text has no test.

variants.title: Unrequested change to the publication gate; it blocks text that needs exactly 5 decode rounds, even with an empty denylist
variants.detail: privateMatches is the shared denylist check used by the publication gates (audit.ts, engine checkPrivateText, repos.ts blob scan, github-notifier, land queue). The diff makes it decode repeatedly and adds \uXXXX unescaping. If decoding hasn't settled after 5 rounds, it returns a synthetic entry 0, which blocks publication. The loop also gives up one round early: after the 5th decode it never checks whether a 6th would be stable, so input that settles after exactly 5 decodes is rejected. Entry 0 is returned even when private-strings.txt is empty. The MCP/digest feature didn't need this change to publication gating, and it makes the change bigger than the ~200-line budget.

variants.title: Unrequested change to publication-gate semantics: nested encodings now block publication even with an empty denylist
variants.detail: privateMatches now decodes repeatedly: percent-encoding plus a new `\\+u` Unicode-escape pass, for up to 5 rounds. If the text is still changing after that, it returns a synthetic entry 0, so checkPrivateText, checkPrivateRange and blob scans block publication even when private-strings.txt is empty. Before this change, an empty denylist never blocked. These functions gate every commit, patch and blob the factory publishes, and the request (MCP tools plus a digest) didn't ask to change them. The extra layers also add up to 6× the text to NFKC-normalize on large diffs.

variants.title: Unrequested change to the publication gate now blocks on deep encoding even with an empty denylist
variants.detail: `privateMatches` now repeatedly decodes `%xx` and literal `\uXXXX` escapes. After 5 rounds it returns a synthetic entry 0, and that entry is returned even when `private-strings.txt` is empty. `audit.ts` (every added diff line) and `repos.ts` (blob scanning) both consume this, so an MCP/digest feature now changes when publication is blocked for every run. This is outside the scope of the request (MCP tools and digest) and roughly doubles the size of the diff in security-sensitive code.

variants.title: When the privacy policy can't be read, every existing MCP tool, including successful mutations, returns only 'output withheld'
variants.detail: The CallTool handler now runs every tool result through loadOutputPrivacy. If private-strings.txt can't be read (bad UTF-8, permissions), all tools except limitless_status return {message:'Tool output withheld'}. That includes create_run after it has created the run, so the agent never gets the new run's id. Previously these tools returned their results directly. This changes how all nine existing tools behave, which the request didn't ask for, and it hides the id needed to inspect a mutation instead of retrying it.

variants.title: Unreadable privacy policy hides create_run/land results after the mutation succeeded
variants.detail: CallTool now replaces every tool's output except limitless_status with 'Tool output withheld; privacy policy unavailable.' when loadOutputPrivacy() returns null, for example when private-strings.txt is not valid UTF-8 or can't be read. The mutation has still run by then. create_run has queued a run and land has queued an entry, but the agent never receives the id. limitless_status in that state also returns neither the requested plain-language state nor the next action, only land id/state and a question count, even though both strings are generated constants.

variants.title: Short registered credentials cause substring withholding of whole MCP output fields
variants.detail: `loadOutputPrivacy` passes every registered credential to `privateMatches`, which does a case-insensitive substring match. `redactCredentials` deliberately skips substring redaction for secrets under 8 characters to avoid false positives. The new path bypasses that guard and replaces the entire field with `[withheld: private text]`. Because `createMcpServer` now applies this to the output of every tool (including keys), existing tools such as get_run and feed are affected as well as the new ones.

variants.title: All MCP tool outputs, including pre-existing tools, are now filtered by the private-strings publication denylist
variants.detail: The CallTool handler now runs `privateOutputData(result, privacy)` on every tool result. It also replaces the whole result with `{message: "Tool output withheld; privacy policy unavailable."}` when private-strings.txt can't be read. This changes the existing create_run, get_run, list_runs, feed, answer and resolve tools, which the request never asked for. private-strings.txt is documented (docs/GUIDE.md) as a publication guard for audit, delivery and land, not as a filter on the local operator's own agent. Any string field that contains a listed value is replaced wholesale, as are object keys. A user who lists their private org or hostname (the documented use) loses repo names, prompts, PR U

variants.title: limitless_status gives no state or next action when the privacy policy cannot be read
variants.detail: When `loadOutputPrivacy()` returns null, `explainStatus` returns only `{land, openQuestions}` and drops `state` and `nextAction`. Those are generated, constant strings that contain no untrusted text, so the tool loses its purpose for no privacy benefit.

variants.title: limitless_status drops state and nextAction when the privacy policy is unreadable
variants.detail: When `privacy` is null, `result()` returns only `{land:{id,state}, openQuestions}`. It omits the plain-language state and next action, which are the tool's whole purpose under the request. Most of those are fixed strings generated by the code itself.

variants.title: Digest makes 1–2 API calls for every distinct run in the unread feed, sequentially, inside a SessionStart hook
variants.detail: For each grouped item, the digest fetches /api/runs/:id and, if the run has a PR, /api/land?run=, one request at a time. If the consumer has never acked (the suggested hook uses --consumer claude), the cursor is at 0 and every retained run with a question, failure, PR or review event is fetched one by one, which slows session start.

variants.title: Digest makes up to two sequential HTTP requests per distinct run in the SessionStart hook
variants.detail: After paging the whole feed since the cursor, the digest fetches `/api/runs/:id` and `/api/land?run=` sequentially for every distinct run across all three groups. A consumer that has never acknowledged (the default `claude` consumer in the suggested hook) scans the whole retained feed. That can mean hundreds of serial requests before the session starts.

variants.title: Approved PRs with no saved head observation are counted as awaiting review
variants.detail: `approval.sha !== pr?.headRefOid` is true when there is no prSnapshot, so a PR with a fresh valid approval is still listed under 'PRs awaiting review'. In the same case limitless_status reports 'PR state unknown', so the two outputs disagree.

variants.title: GET /api/land?run=<unknown> throws a generic Error and likely returns 500 instead of 404
variants.detail: `list(runId)` throws `new Error("run not found")`. The HTTP handler has no mapping for it, unlike the other run routes, which return `error("run not found", 404)`.

variants.title: MCP review approvals are recorded as reviewer "human"
variants.detail: The limitless_review input schema is strict and leaves out `reviewer`. The call passes `ReviewVerdictSchema.parse(input)` without one, and submitReview then falls back to `parsed.data.reviewer ?? "human"` (src/pipeline/review-round.ts:193). So an approval an AI agent submits over MCP is stored in review_approvals as reviewer "human". The review.approved feed trigger then shows it as "approved at <sha> by human". Other paths label their source: the CLI sends `reviewer: process.env.USER ?? "cli"`, and MCP's own answer tool sends `by: "mcp"`. This approval is what lets limitless_land merge, so the audit trail misattributes who approved a merge.

variants.title: Digest caps the line count but not line length
variants.detail: Each row embeds the full quoted title and summary, and for questions the full question text. Land-blocked reasons and question bodies can be long, so the "at most 20 lines" SessionStart output can still inject a large block into every new session's context.

head: b0cfa54363d9d9e79509e06bf471245113d5467b
prompt:
Closes #36. Enforce model-origin exclusions in the router, not only in eval policy.

## Why
`[routing] exclude_origins` in config.toml is parsed today only by `src/evals/settings.ts` and honoured only by `src/evals/policy.ts` (a model is excluded when its `origin` or `baseOrigin` is listed, or when its `baseOrigin` is "unknown" while a list is configured). The runtime `Router` (src/router/router.ts) ignores it, so when subscription quotas ran out, review and verify calls fell back to a CN-origin model even though the policy work assumed such models were excluded. At work, CN-origin models must never be called.

## What
1. One shared parser for `[routing] exclude_origins` (reuse it in `evalSettings`; the semantics above stay identical, including "unknown baseOrigin is excluded when a list is configured"). No exclusion when the key is absent (today's behaviour at home stays unchanged).
2. The Router treats an excluded model as ineligible on every route: policy cells, out-of-cell fallbacks, the free-first and vendor-avoidance fallbacks, escalation, panel and verifier selection, and models added at runtime (`catalog add`, discovery). The skip reason in the run log and in `routing preview` reads `origin excluded (<origin>; baseOrigin=<baseOrigin>)`. There is NO fallback to an excluded model: when exclusions leave no candidate, the invocation fails with that reason.
3. Explicit choices are refused up front, never silently skipped: `run --model role=…` and `retry --model`, `routing set`, the Setup tab's routing and fallback saves (HTTP 400 with the reason), `catalog add` of an excluded origin (allowed to add, but `catalog list` marks it excluded and routing never picks it), and `eval run --models` (refuses excluded models with the reason before any trial starts).
4. Visibility: `routing show`, `catalog list` and the Setup tab show the configured exclusions (read-only; changing them stays a config.toml edit plus restart, on purpose: it is a safety constraint).
5. Docs: document the key and its semantics where routing config is documented.

## Tests (fake harness only; read test/AGENTS.md)
- A fallback that would reach an excluded model when every allowed provider is exhausted fails with the reason instead (this is the regression).
- Each refusal path above (run pin, retry pin, routing set, HTTP setup save, eval run) rejects an excluded model; a model whose baseOrigin is "unknown" is excluded only when a list is configured.
- With no `exclude_origins`, routing is byte-for-byte unchanged (existing routing tests keep passing).

Budget: about 200 changed source lines plus tests. Out of scope: per-repo or per-role exclusion lists, live editing of the list.

The new diagnostic handling in RunContext.invoke does not cover this separate invocation path.

variants.detail: The exclusion check runs after the production panel selects one verifier. In src/pipeline/engine.ts:1336–1342, every configured verifier enters pickVerifier, and the chosen target is offered alone through `only`. An excluded first verifier therefore causes NoCapacityError even when a later allowed verifier is available. A focused Bun probe using the existing pickVerifier function and real Router returned `selected: openrouter/deepseek-v4-pro`, an empty selectedRoute with `origin excluded (CN; baseOrigin=CN)`, and a nonempty allowedRoute for codex/sol.

variants.title: Eval resume doesn't check stored switch chains for excluded origins before trials start
variants.detail: `resume()` checks each stored switch-chain target with `router.resolveFor`, which doesn't look at origin. If `exclude_origins` was added after the original eval ran, the resume is accepted. The excluded model is only caught when `nextImplementTarget` calls `router.toTarget`, which throws after round one has already run on another model, so that trial ends in an error instead of being refused with the reason before any trial starts. The excluded model is never called, so safety holds, but this doesn't match the 'refused up front'

variants.detail: The 'exhausted providers' regression test asserts that `route()` returns no candidates and skips `openrouter/ds` with the origin reason. The request asks for a test that the invocation fails with the reason.

variants.title: No test for the regression at the invocation level (NoCapacityError with the origin reason)
variants.detail: The request's main regression test is: when every allowed provider is exhausted, the invocation fails with the origin reason. The new tests only check Router.route(), which returns no candidates plus a skipped entry. None of them drives RunContext's invoke loop, so the new code in context.ts is never run: the warn log, the reason in the NoCapacityError message, and the privateOutput variant.

variants.title: Private-output error repeats the same origin reason
variants.detail: The warn log removes duplicate origin reasons with `new Set`, but the privateOutput NoCapacityError joins the raw `origins` array. When several skipped models share an origin, the same 'origin excluded (CN; baseOrigin=CN)' text appears several times in the message.

variants.title: Private-output error repeats identical origin reasons
variants.detail: The run-log warning dedupes origin reasons with `new Set`, but the privateOutput NoCapacityError message joins the raw `origins` array, so the same `origin excluded (...)` text can appear several times.

variants.title: Private-output no-capacity message repeats the same origin reason
variants.detail: The run-log warning deduplicates the origin reasons with `new Set`, but the `privateOutput` NoCapacityError message joins the raw `origins` array. When several CN models are skipped, it repeats `origin excluded (CN; baseOrigin=CN)` once per skipped model.

variants.title: Awkward manual line wrap in docs paragraph
variants.detail: The new paragraph breaks after 'Excluded models are never', leaving a short line, while the surrounding prose is wrapped at about 100 columns.

variants.title: Configured [review.rosters] finder pins to an excluded model aren't refused at startup
variants.detail: `checkRosterTargets` checks roster targets for transport and local/free problems at startup but doesn't check origin. If a production roster pins a finder to an excluded-origin model, the router correctly skips it at runtime. But in panel mode a non-local pinned finder then fails every review with NoCapacityError, and a local one is silently dropped as FinderSkipped. The operator only finds out when a review runs. Roster pins aren't among the request's listed refusal paths, so this is a gap in the spirit of item 3 rather than a missed requirement.

head: 5a57b035e284b98bd84a2483519bed208135cecb
prompt:
## Problem
One of the deprecated implicit providers in the built-in catalog is named after a specific machine on the owner's network. It is the llama.cpp provider listed beside `omlx` and `mtplx` (see the comment above the implicit defaults in `src/router/catalog.ts`). Its id, label, model id and default base URLs (`http://<that host>:8080`) put a private hostname into public code. The same name runs through the `limitless local` command (`src/cli/local.ts`, its `[local]` config keys and help text), routing policy, docs, scripts and tests. AGENTS.md's privacy rule says the repository must never carry hostnames or machine names from the owner's setup.

No configuration uses this provider: the owner's config defines nothing for it, and it is disabled at runtime. The other two implicit providers are named after software, not machines.

## Change
1. Remove the machine-named provider and its model from the built-in catalog and its implicit defaults. A LAN llama.cpp server is still supported, but only as a config-defined provider (`[[providers]]` with `kind = "openai-compatible"` and its own `base_url`). Add a short example to docs/GUIDE.md using placeholders (`<host>`, `example.com`).
2. Remove it from every routing chain in `routing/policy.json` and from `routing/overrides.json` / `routing/EVIDENCE.md`. Describe history with neutral wording (for example "a LAN llama.cpp host").
3. `limitless local`: keep the remote llama.cpp management, but under neutral names. Config keys become, for example, `[local].remote_host`, `remote_model_path` and `remote_llama_binary`, with the host required and no default. If no host is configured, `local up` / `status` report only oMLX. Update the help text.
4. Records written before the change still render and resume. Runs, invocations, eval results and runtime provider state can reference the removed provider or model id. Handle unknown ids generically, without keeping the old name in code (no entry for it in a removed-models list). Check `limitless eval report`, run pages, provider listings and routing resolution against a database that contains the old ids.
5. Neutral wording everywhere else the name appears in code, scripts, tests and docs: README.md, docs/*.md (including docs/research), scripts/smoke.ts, scripts/seed-demo.ts and test files outside `test/fixtures/`.

Don't write the machine's name in the PR title, body, commit messages or new text. Call it "the machine-named provider".

## Tests
- The built-in catalog and routing policy contain no provider or model with that name. Add a test that fails if a hostname-like default base URL (one that isn't localhost, 127.0.0.1 or a documented public API host) appears in the built-in catalog.
- A config-defined openai-compatible provider for a LAN host routes and health-checks as before.
- `limitless local status` with and without `[local].remote_host`.
- A database containing runs, invocations and eval trials with the old ids still renders them, and routing doesn't fail.

## Out of scope
- `evals/*/cases.json` (historical eval case content; changing it changes eval cache keys).
- Captured files under `test/fixtures/` (a protected path). If a test depends on one that mentions the name, add a new fixture file or build the data inline, and say so in the report.
- `PROMPT.md` (the owner's original brief) and git history.

## Budget
About 120 changed lines of source and scripts (mostly deletions), plus tests and docs.

Output: TypeError: Invalid URL; SSH calls:

variants.title: Unvalidated remote_host can crash `limitless local` with a raw TypeError
variants.detail: The code builds `new URL(`http://${host}:8080`)` from `[local].remote_host` without catching errors. Hosts that are valid SSH destinations but not valid URL hosts make the URL constructor throw `TypeError: Invalid URL`. That aborts the whole command, including the oMLX report that was already worked out.

variants.detail: manageLocal builds `new URL(`http://${host}:8080`)` with no error handling. If `remote_host` is an IPv6 literal (a valid ssh target) or contains a character URLs reject, the call throws TypeError: Invalid URL. The whole command then fails, including the oMLX report that was already computed. Before this change, a bad host only made the remote endpoint report "unreachable", because fetch errors were caught.

variants.title: The configured provider is only found when the SSH destination matches the provider's HTTP origin

prompt:
## Problem
One of the deprecated implicit providers in the built-in catalog is named after a specific machine on the owner's network. It is the llama.cpp provider listed beside `omlx` and `mtplx` (see the comment above the implicit defaults in `src/router/catalog.ts`). Its id, label, model id and default base URLs (`http://<that host>:8080`) put a private hostname into public code. The same name runs through the `limitless local` command (`src/cli/local.ts`, its `[local]` config keys and help text), routing policy, docs, scripts and tests. AGENTS.md's privacy rule says the repository must never carry hostnames or machine names from the owner's setup.

No configuration uses this provider: the owner's config defines nothing for it, and it is disabled at runtime. The other two implicit providers are named after software, not machines.

## Change
1. Remove the machine-named provider and its model from the built-in catalog and its implicit defaults. A LAN llama.cpp server is still supported, but only as a config-defined provider (`[[providers]]` with `kind = "openai-compatible"` and its own `base_url`). Add a short example to docs/GUIDE.md using placeholders (`<host>`, `example.com`).
2. Remove it from every routing chain in `routing/policy.json` and from `routing/overrides.json` / `routing/EVIDENCE.md`. Describe history with neutral wording (for example "a LAN llama.cpp host").
3. `limitless local`: keep the remote llama.cpp management, but under neutral names. Config keys become, for example, `[local].remote_host`, `remote_model_path` and `remote_llama_binary`, with the host required and no default. If no host is configured, `local up` / `status` report only oMLX. Update the help text.
4. Records written before the change still render and resume. Runs, invocations, eval results and runtime provider state can reference the removed provider or model id. Handle unknown ids generically, without keeping the old name in code (no entry for it in a removed-models list). Check `limitless eval report`, run pages, provider listings and routing resolution against a database that contains the old ids.
5. Neutral wording everywhere else the name appears in code, scripts, tests and docs: README.md, docs/*.md (including docs/research), scripts/smoke.ts, scripts/seed-demo.ts and test files outside `test/fixtures/`.

Don't write the machine's name in the PR title, body, commit messages or new text. Call it "the machine-named provider".

## Tests
- The built-in catalog and routing policy contain no provider or model with that name. Add a test that fails if a hostname-like default base URL (one that isn't localhost, 127.0.0.1 or a documented public API host) appears in the built-in catalog.
- A config-defined openai-compatible provider for a LAN host routes and health-checks as before.
- `limitless local status` with and without `[local].remote_host`.
- A database containing runs, invocations and eval trials with the old ids still renders them, and routing doesn't fail.

## Out of scope
- `evals/*/cases.json` (historical eval case content; changing it changes eval cache keys).
- Captured files under `test/fixtures/` (a protected path). If a test depends on one that mentions the name, add a new fixture file or build the data inline, and say so in the report.
- `PROMPT.md` (the owner's original brief) and git history.

## Budget
About 120 changed lines of source and scripts (mostly deletions), plus tests and docs.

variants.detail: `local up` and `local down` find the provider whose `openaiBaseUrl` origin equals `http://<remote_host>:8080`. In all three, no provider is matched. Then the health probe goes out without the API key, so llama-server answers 401 and the endpoint shows 'unreachable', and enablement is never updated. `docs/OPERATIONS.md` documents the limitation, but the failure is silent.

variants.title: `local up/down` finds the configured provider only on port 8080 of exactly `remote_host`
variants.detail: `remoteProvider` is found by comparing the origin `http://${remote_host}:8080` with each provider's openaiBaseUrl. variants.title: Generic retired-ID filtering also silences previously explicit startup errors (owner-decision removals, model-id-in-prefer)

variants.title: Over the ~120-line source budget, partly from extra scope
variants.detail: About 260 lines of source changed against the requested budget of about 120. The new `unavailable` listing in the routing snapshot and the Setup UI rendering go beyond what the request asked for.

variants.title: Catalog-edit validation was relaxed beyond retired references, and the change is over budget

Together with the Setup.tsx UI additions and the new `unavailable` snapshot fields, source changes are about 250 lines against the requested ~120.

variants.title: Smoke no longer covers any LAN llama.cpp provider

prompt:
## Problem
Gate output is untrusted text produced by the change under test, and it leaves the process unredacted. `runGates` (`src/gates/run.ts`) keeps a tail of each check's combined output, and that text is:
- stored as JSON in the run's artifacts, state and the gate cache (SQLite);
- written to land queue logs (`<private-path><run>/land-<id>.log`);
- included in the deploy gate's error;
- sent to models in the implementer's gate feedback (`formatGateFeedback`) and in review and verify prompts.

None of these paths calls `redactCredentials`. A review of #408 confirmed it with synthetic registered credentials: they survived storage, implementer feedback and the deploy error unchanged. AGENTS.md requires redaction at every boundary where secret-bearing text is stored or sent to a model. Gate commands get an environment without factory secrets, but a check can still print a credential it reads some other way, and an honest test failure can echo one from a fixture or an error message.

## Change
- Redact gate output once, where `runGates` builds a check's result (before the tail is cut and before failure excerpts from #408 are extracted, so a secret split by the cut is still caught: decode/redact first, truncate after). Every consumer then receives redacted text from that single place.
- Check every path that reads raw command output before that point (for example the confinement-error scan in `launchFailure`, which must keep seeing the raw text) and confirm none of them stores or forwards it.
- The deploy gate in `src/cli/service.ts` builds its own tails; redact them the same way, through the same helper.

## Tests
- A check whose output contains a registered credential, including one that straddles the tail boundary and one inside a failure excerpt: the stored gate result, the land log, the implementer feedback, the review/verify prompt text and the deploy error contain the redaction marker, not the value.
- Confinement-error detection still works on output that also contains a credential.

## Budget
About 30 net source lines, plus tests.

## Out of scope
- Redaction of other command output (agent tool results are already redacted by the harnesses).
- Changing what gates may read.

Now every result carries `confinementError: false`. The diff also changes `confinementFailed` so that an explicit false skips the backstop scan of the output. Every result now carries `confinementError: false`. The schema in this repo (evals/cases.ts) accepts that, but the documented reason for the old behaviour was dropped without explanation. The change was made only so that `??` in confinementFailed can skip the output scan.

- stored as JSON in the run's artifacts, state and the gate cache (SQLite);
- written to land queue logs (`<private-path><run>/land-<id>.log`);
- included in the deploy gate's error;
- sent to models in the implementer's gate feedback (`formatGateFeedback`) and in review and verify prompts.

None of these paths calls `redactCredentials`. A review of #408 confirmed it with synthetic registered credentials: they survived storage, implementer feedback and the deploy error unchanged. AGENTS.md requires redaction at every boundary where secret-bearing text is stored or sent to a model. Gate commands get an environment without factory secrets, but a check can still print a credential it reads some other way, and an honest test failure can echo one from a fixture or an error message.

## Change
- Redact gate output once, where `runGates` builds a check's result (before the tail is cut and before failure excerpts from #408 are extracted, so a secret split by the cut is still caught: decode/redact first, truncate after). Every consumer then receives redacted text from that single place.
- Check every path that reads raw command output before that point (for example the confinement-error scan in `launchFailure`, which must keep seeing the raw text) and confirm none of them stores or forwards it.
- The deploy gate in `src/cli/service.ts` builds its own tails; redact them the same way, through the same helper.

## Tests
- A check whose output contains a registered credential, including one that straddles the tail boundary and one inside a failure excerpt: the stored gate result, the land log, the implementer feedback, the review/verify prompt text and the deploy error contain the redaction marker, not the value.
- Confinement-error detection still works on output that also contains a credential.

## Budget
About 30 net source lines, plus tests.

## Out of scope
- Redaction of other command output (agent tool results are already redacted by the harnesses).
- Changing what gates may read.

prompt:
Closes #36. Enforce model-origin exclusions in the router, not only in eval policy.

## Why
`[routing] exclude_origins` in config.toml is parsed today only by `src/evals/settings.ts` and honoured only by `src/evals/policy.ts` (a model is excluded when its `origin` or `baseOrigin` is listed, or when its `baseOrigin` is "unknown" while a list is configured). The runtime `Router` (src/router/router.ts) ignores it, so when subscription quotas ran out, review and verify calls fell back to a CN-origin model even though the policy work assumed such models were excluded. At work, CN-origin models must never be called.

## What
1. One shared parser for `[routing] exclude_origins` (reuse it in `evalSettings`; the semantics above stay identical, including "unknown baseOrigin is excluded when a list is configured"). No exclusion when the key is absent (today's behaviour at home stays unchanged).
2. The Router treats an excluded model as ineligible on every route: policy cells, out-of-cell fallbacks, the free-first and vendor-avoidance fallbacks, escalation, panel and verifier selection, and models added at runtime (`catalog add`, discovery). The skip reason in the run log and in `routing preview` reads `origin excluded (<origin>; baseOrigin=<baseOrigin>)`. There is NO fallback to an excluded model: when exclusions leave no candidate, the invocation fails with that reason.
3. Fixes #407.

## Problem
A failing check's output is cut to its end before anyone reads it. `runGates` keeps only the last 6,000 characters of a check's combined output (`src/gates/run.ts`, `OUTPUT_TAIL`); `formatGateFeedback` (`src/pipeline/prompts.ts`) sends the implementer the last 3,000 of those; the deploy gate (`src/cli/service.ts`) keeps stdout/stderr tails too.

`bun test` prints each failure's details (source excerpt, `error:` line, expected/received diff, stack) in the per-file section, just before that test's `(fail)` line. At the end of a long run it prints only the skipped-test list, the names of the failed tests and the counts. With this repository's ~3,000-test suite the tail therefore names the failing test without saying why it failed, in:
- the land queue log (`<private-path><run>/land-<id>.log`): land 1 for #405 blocked on `test failed`, and the log shows only `(fail) land publishes its pinned SHA from an isolated push repository: push-failed`;
- the deploy gate's error (seen on 10-04: one failing test, unnamed);
- the implementer's gate feedback, so implementers re-run the full suite to find the assertion (part of the background-test polling behind #406).

## Change
1. One shared helper (for example in `src/gates/run.ts`) that extracts failure excerpts from test output: for each bun `(fail)` line and each TAP `not ok` line (ANSI control sequences stripped, as `formatGateFeedback` already does), the lines before it back to the previous test result line or file header (`<path>.test.ts:`). Cap it: at most 40 lines per failure, the first 10 failures, about 8,000 characters in total, and say when something was left out.
2. Gate results carry the excerpts in a new optional field (for example `failures?: string`), set only for a failed check. `output` stays the tail, unchanged. The field is additive: persisted results without it render as before.
3. Every consumer that shows a failed check uses the excerpts before the tail: the land queue log, the deploy gate's error, and `formatGateFeedback` (excerpts first, then a shorter tail, within a similar total size).
4. The excerpts follow exactly the same redaction and storage path as `output` does today; don't add a second path.

## Tests
- Bun-format output built inline in the test (don't edit captured files under `test/fixtures/`, which is a protected path), with the failing block more than 6,000 characters before the end: the gate result's excerpt contains the `error:` line and the diff, and the implementer feedback, the land log and the deploy error contain them.
- Several failures, the caps and the "left out" note; TAP `not ok`; a passing check (no field); ANSI-colored output.
- A gate result without the new field (an older release's) still formats.

## Budget
About 80 net source lines, plus tests.

## Out of scope
- Raising `OUTPUT_TAIL` or storing full output in the database.
- Formats other than bun's `(fail)` and TAP `not ok`.
- Changing how the land queue or deploy decide pass or fail.

# Resume: record trusted Git paths for worktrees created before #323

## What happened (2026-10-04, deploying #323)
After the restart onto #323, every run whose worktree had been created by the previous release failed on its next git call with `Missing trusted Git paths`:
- 3 fix runs failed;
- 1 needs_human run failed at delivery after its work was done.

#323's hardened wrapper (`trustedEnv`, src/git/command.ts) refuses a linked worktree without a `<worktree>.git-paths` record. Only `createWorktree` writes that record, so worktrees made before the upgrade never get one. The same check broke `scripts/land-pr.sh`'s private check in linked worktrees; that is fixed on #316's branch.

The work wasn't lost: the commits sat in the worktrees and were salvaged by hand.

## Fix
- When a run resumes and its worktree is a linked worktree with no record, record it once (`recordWorktree`). Log that this happened.
  - An agent confined by #323 can't delete the record, because the record sits outside the writable checkout. So a missing record means the worktree predates the upgrade.
  - The resumed run gets no less trust than it had before the upgrade.
- Alternatively, record every existing worktree from a migration step at daemon start.

## Acceptance
- A run whose worktree has no record is parked, then resumed under the new code. It finishes, with exactly one "recorded legacy worktree" log line.
- A worktree whose record exists but no longer matches still fails closed ("Unsafe worktree Git administration").

Budget: ≤ 20 changed source lines plus a test. Low priority: on this machine every affected run has been handled. It matters for the next install that upgrades with runs in flight.

Tracking issue: #357.

Draft delivery and interrupted preparation can reuse a legacy worktree before path registration.

variants.detail: Recovery only examines ctx.state.worktreePath. During preparation, createWorktree creates the checkout before that path is persisted. If the old daemon stops in that interval, the resumed run has an existing legacy worktree but no saved worktreePath. This check skips it, and createWorktree's reuse branch immediately calls worktreeGit, which fails with "Missing trusted Git paths".

variants.detail: The check only looks at `ctx.state.worktreePath`. In `prepare`, `worktreePath` is set after `createWorktree` but only saved several git calls later (mergeReviewBase/resetTo/discardChanges/readFileAt). Take a pre-upgrade run restarted in that window: it resumes in phase prepare with no worktreePath. `createWorktree` then sees the directory exists and calls `worktreeGit(["git","rev-parse","HEAD"])`, which throws "Missing trusted Git paths".

variants.detail: `executeScopedRun` throws `NeedsHumanError(ctx.state.needsHumanReason)` at line 172, before the new recording block at lines 178-186. The catch handler then calls `deliver(ctx, false)` for the worktree (lines 304-317). The worktree still has no `.git-paths` record, so every git call in `trustedEnv` throws "Missing trusted Git paths" and the draft PR is never opened. The incident report names exactly this case: "1 needs_human run failed at delivery after its work was done". The `verifiedFailure` draft path can hit the same problem if anything throws before line 178.

variants.detail: The new test parks the run in phase 'loop' with no needsHumanReason. It doesn't cover resuming at delivery or with needsHumanReason set, which is where the gap above is. The test also deletes the record from a worktree that `createWorktree` set up under the new code, rather than one built the pre-upgrade way. That's acceptable, but it doesn't exercise any other git calls that happen before `executeScopedRun` (for example, scheduler recovery).

# UI: a Setup tab for routing, fallbacks and models

## Why
Parts 1–3 make routing configurable at runtime: per-run model chains, the live operator policy layer, and discovery with runtime catalog additions. The operator needs one place in the UI to see and change all of it without a terminal. Typical tasks:
- reroute a role when a subscription runs low;
- try a newly served model;
- see why a role would route where it does right now.

Depends on parts 1–3.

## What
A new **Setup** page (`/setup`, in the main navigation). It is built on the part 1–3 APIs and updates live over SSE.

1. **Routing grid.** Rows are roles; columns are cells (`default`, `trivial`, `small`, `medium`, `large`; show only the cells a role uses, plus "add cell").
   - Each cell shows its chain as ordered groups of model chips. A chip shows the model id, effort, provider and billing (free, subscription, metered).
   - Each cell has a source badge: code, evals or yours.
   - Where you override the evals value, show the evals value next to yours, so drift from the recommendation stays visible.
   - **Editing:** add, remove and reorder groups; add an alternative within a group; choose the effort from the model's supported efforts; add an optional note.
   - Validation errors from the API appear inline. Save writes the operator cell. "Reset to recommended" deletes it.
   - The provider preference list is editable the same way.
2. **Right now.** For each cell, the live preview: the model a call would use now, and each skipped candidate with its reason (exhausted until …, over reserve, disabled, unhealthy, not served). Include each subscription provider's quota headroom, so the operator can plan around exhaustion.
3. **Models.**
   - The catalog, with each model's source (code, config, runtime).
   - The discovered **served but not in the catalog** list per provider. Each entry has an "Add" form that prefills the backend name; origin, vendor and tier are required.
   - **Catalog but not served** warnings.
   - Edit and delete for runtime-added models, with the API's refusal shown when a policy cell references the model.
4. **Providers.** Reuse the existing provider cards (enable, disable, fast mode) on this page.
5. **History.** Recent routing and catalog changes: what, old → new, note, when.
6. **Run surfaces.**
   - The New Run form's "Models" section uses the same chain picker as the grid.
   - Run detail gets **Retry with different models…**, which opens the picker prefilled with the run's chains and calls the retry endpoint with the replacement map.
7. The Models page keeps its stats. Its read-only policy rendering is replaced by a link to Setup.

Usable at phone width with no horizontal page scroll. Match the existing UI style and components.

## Tests
Follow `test/AGENTS.md` and the existing UI test patterns, with fake API responses:
- the grid renders layers and badges;
- an edit sends the right `PUT` and shows a validation error;
- reset sends `DELETE`;
- the preview renders skip reasons;
- the Add form requires origin and submits the prefilled backend name;
- Retry with different models sends the replacement map;
- an SSE `routing` message updates the grid.

Budget: about 450 changed source lines, plus tests.

Tracking issue: #375. Parts 1-3 have landed: #380 (per-run model chains, CLI --model and the retry replacement map), #378 (live operator policy: GET/PUT/DELETE /api/routing, preview, history, SSE routing messages) and #387 (discovery and the runtime catalog: GET /api/catalog, POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/catalog/models). Build the UI on those APIs; read their handlers in src/server/http.ts before designing.

Closes #402. After the checks, `scripts/land-pr.sh` must not run git against the land clone's repository configuration.

## Why
`scripts/land-pr.sh` runs the PR's own code unconfined (`bun install` lifecycle scripts, `bun run check`) and then still runs git in the land clone: `safe_git add -A`, `diff --cached --quiet`, `commit`, `status --porcelain`, `rev-parse`. Repository config written by that code can make these run commands (#402): a clean filter added after `safe_git` enumerated filter keys (a race), `diff.external` with `diff.trustExitCode`, `commit.gpgSign` with `gpg.program`, `core.pager` with `pager.add` under a terminal, and git errors that print config values. #401 already pushes from an isolated repository for the same reason.

## What
1. **No staging or committing in the land script.** Remove the post-check `add -A` / staged-diff / commit block. Landing requires that everything is already committed (merges included: the orchestrator commits merges before landing). After the checks, refuse to land if a merge is in progress (`MERGE_HEAD`, `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, `REVERT_HEAD` exist under the recorded admin dir; check the files directly, not via git) or the work tree differs from the commit being landed.
2. **Isolated dirty check and SHA.** Read the pinned SHA before the checks run (from the recorded, trusted paths, as today). After the checks, create the same kind of private temporary bare repository #401 creates (alternates to the clone's objects), and run the dirty check there: `git --git-dir="$iso" --work-tree="$clone" read-tree "$sha"` with a private index file (GIT_INDEX_FILE inside the temp dir), then `status --porcelain --untracked-files=normal` (and `--ignored=no`) with the same hardening flags; any output refuses the land. Clone-level filter, diff, pager and signing configuration never apply because the git dir is the isolated one; GLOBAL/SYSTEM config still applies as usual. Reuse the isolated repository for the push (#401) instead of creating a second one.
3. **No config values in messages.** Every lookup in the post-check path reports a generic message instead of raw git diagnostics.
4. Keep everything else (scans, private-string checks, CI wait, merge via gh, the exact-SHA pin, #401's push protocol policy).

## Tests (test/land-pr.test.ts; existing fakes; no network; CI runners have git-lfs filters configured globally, don't assert full argv; read test/AGENTS.md)
- Each of: a clean filter added during the checks (and one added right before the dirty check via the fake gh step), `diff.external`+`diff.trustExitCode`, `commit.gpgSign`+`gpg.program`, `core.pager`+`pager.status` with a pseudo-terminal if practical (otherwise assert `GIT_PAGER`/`--no-pager` use), planted in the clone's config: no marker runs and the land still succeeds on a clean tree.
- A tracked file modified by the checks, an untracked non-ignored file created by the checks, and an in-progress merge each refuse the land without pushing.
- A malformed include in the clone's config after the checks does not print its value.
Each new test fails with its part reverted.

Budget: about 40 changed source lines plus tests (net, given the removed commit block). Out of scope: the land queue and delivery paths (their metadata is not writable by confined code).

gold.summary: The isolated post-check status still inspects populated submodules with their own git directories, so a submodule that points at the land clone's admin directory runs a clean filter from the clone's configuration, which the request says never applies after the checks.

variants.title: Writing info/exclude assumes `git init` created info/ from templates
variants.detail: `printf '%s' "$exclude" > "$push_repo/info/exclude"` needs the info/ directory. That directory comes only from the init template; objects/info is always created, but info/ is not. If a user's global config sets `init.templateDir` to a directory without info/, or a packaged git has no template dir, the redirect fails and `set -e` stops every land with a raw bash error.

variants.title: Writing info/exclude fails when the global init.templateDir has no info/ directory
variants.detail: `printf '%s' "$exclude" > "$push_repo/info/exclude"` assumes `git init --bare` created `info/`. That only happens when the template dir has one. With a global `init.templateDir` pointing at a hooks-only template (e.g. the git-secrets setup), `init --bare` creates only HEAD, config, objects and refs (verified: `git -c init.templateDir=$TMPDIR/empty init --bare tdt` gives no info/). The redirect fails, and under `set -e` the script exits with a raw shell 'No such file or directory' instead of a generic refusal. It fails safe, but no land can succeed for that user. The #401 push repo never wrote under info/, so this is new.

variants.title: Writing `info/exclude` fails when git init uses an empty template directory
variants.detail: The line `printf '%s' "$exclude" > "$push_repo/info/exclude"` assumes `git init --bare` created `info/`. That directory comes from the init template. With an empty template (for example a global `init.templateDir` pointing at an empty directory, or `--template=`), `info/` does not exist. I confirmed that `git init --bare --template=` creates only HEAD, config, objects and refs. The redirect then fails, `set -e` aborts the land with a raw shell error, and this step skips the script's usual checked-step handling with a generic message.

variants.title: Dirty check on a fresh index re-hashes every file, so files that rely on a global filter (such as git-lfs) would show as modified
variants.detail: read-tree fills the private index with no stat data, so status re-hashes every tracked file. safe_git disables all filter.* keys, including global ones like filter.lfs.clean. A smudged LFS file in the work tree would therefore hash differently from its pointer blob and be reported as modified, which refuses the land. Before this change, the clone's index kept stat data and avoided the re-hash. This repository has no .gitattributes, so nothing breaks today. The request did ask for these same hardening flags.

variants.title: Fresh index without stat data makes smudged LFS files look modified
variants.detail: After `read-tree`, the private index has no stat data, so `status` hashes every work-tree file. `safe_git` blanks every `filter.*` key, including the global `filter.lfs.*` ones, so files that LFS smudged on checkout hash to their real contents, not their pointer blobs. They therefore show as modified and the land is refused. The old in-clone status used an index with cached stat data and would not have hashed them. This repository has no tracked `.gitattributes` or LFS files today, so there is no current impact.

variants.title: The pager scenario runs without a terminal and never checks for `--no-pager`
variants.detail: The request asked for a pseudo-terminal or, failing that, an assertion that `GIT_PAGER`/`--no-pager` is used. The `checks:pager` scenario plants core.pager and pager.status but runs without a TTY, and git never starts a pager without one. So the scenario passes even if both `--no-pager` and the isolation are removed. Only the separate assertion that post-check calls use the private git dir would catch a regression.

variants.title: The pager scenario can never trigger the pager, and `--no-pager` is untested
variants.detail: The `checks:pager` scenario plants `core.pager` and `pager.status`, but the script captures status output with `dirty="$(...)"`, and the test runs without a pseudo-terminal. Git only starts a pager when stdout is a terminal, so no marker could run even with the old in-clone status or with `--no-pager` removed. The request asked for a pseudo-terminal or, failing that, an assertion that `GIT_PAGER` or `--no-pager` is used. The test does neither, so removing the new `--no-pager` from `safe_git` would not fail any test. Only the general 'post-check git uses the private dir' assertion covers isolation here.

variants.title: Late config injection targets the isolated repository
variants.detail: The fake gh process inherits GIT_COMMON_DIR pointing at the isolated repository. Passing --git-dir for the clone does not override that variable, so these config commands modify the isolated repository instead of the clone. A two-repository probe confirmed the setting was absent from the clone and present in the isolated repository. Consequently, the passing pre-push:clean-filter test does not exercise the explicitly requested late clone-config injection.

variants.title: New no-private-strings scenario failed once in a full-file run
variants.detail: In the first full run of test/land-pr.test.ts, the new `no-private-strings` case failed: `expect(pushRepos).toHaveLength(1)` received 0, so the land stopped before the push. Run alone, the scenario passed. The whole isolated-push-repository group then passed 5 times in a row, which points to an intermittent failure under load. I couldn't capture the land script's stderr from the failed run, so I don't know the cause.

variants.title: Source change is well over the ~40-line budget
variants.detail: `land-pr.sh` changes by about +70/−40, plus the edit to `check-private-strings.ts`. The extra lines (exclude snapshot, LFS symlink, HEAD write, checker cwd/env plumbing) are justified by the isolation, but some only explain themselves in brief comments.

prompt:
## Problem
Gate output is untrusted text produced by the change under test, and it leaves the process unredacted. `runGates` (`src/gates/run.ts`) keeps a tail of each check's combined output, and that text is:
- stored as JSON in the run's artifacts, state and the gate cache (SQLite);
- written to land queue logs (`<private-path><run>/land-<id>.log`);
- included in the deploy gate's error;
- sent to models in the implementer's gate feedback (`formatGateFeedback`) and in review and verify prompts.

None of these paths calls `redactCredentials`. A review of #408 confirmed it with synthetic registered credentials: they survived storage, implementer feedback and the deploy error unchanged. AGENTS.md requires redaction at every boundary where secret-bearing text is stored or sent to a model. Gate commands get an environment without factory secrets, but a check can still print a credential it reads some other way, and an honest test failure can echo one from a fixture or an error message.

## Change
- Redact gate output once, where `runGates` builds a check's result (before the tail is cut and before failure excerpts from #408 are extracted, so a secret split by the cut is still caught: decode/redact first, truncate after). Every consumer then receives redacted text from that single place.
- Check every path that reads raw command output before that point (for example the confinement-error scan in `launchFailure`, which must keep seeing the raw text) and confirm none of them stores or forwards it.
- The deploy gate in `src/cli/service.ts` builds its own tails; redact them the same way, through the same helper.

## Tests
- A check whose output contains a registered credential, including one that straddles the tail boundary and one inside a failure excerpt: the stored gate result, the land log, the implementer feedback, the review/verify prompt text and the deploy error contain the redaction marker, not the value.
- Confinement-error detection still works on output that also contains a credential.

## Budget
About 30 net source lines, plus tests.

## Out of scope
- Redaction of other command output (agent tool results are already redacted by the harnesses).
- Changing what gates may read.

variants.detail: The runner replaces complete matches before retaining the overlap. If a registered credential prefixes another, receiving the shorter value first destroys the prefix needed to recognize the longer credential. The longer credential's remaining sensitive suffix is then emitted unchanged. variants.title: Privacy filter now withholds any text containing "[redacted]" in full
variants.detail: `loadOutputPrivacy` now returns "[withheld: private text]" for any string containing the literal "[redacted]". This filter runs on every MCP tool result (`privateOutputData`), on digest output and on `explainStatus`. Now that gate output (and the redaction marker in it) flows into run state, feed text and reasons, a single redacted credential hides the whole field from operators, not just the secret. The same happens to any user or agent text that simply contains the word "[redacted]". The request didn't ask for this, and redaction already removes the value itself.

variants.title: Privacy filter now withholds any text containing the literal "[redacted]"
variants.detail: `loadOutputPrivacy` now returns "[withheld: private text]" for any string containing "[redacted]", whatever its source. The filter is shared by the MCP tools (mcp.ts, mcp-status.ts) and the digest CLI. Harnesses already redact credentials to "[redacted]" in agent tool results and errors, and gate output now does too. So run errors, feedback, terminal reasons and events that used to show their redacted text are now hidden entirely. So is any user prompt that contains the literal token. The request did not ask for this, it lists other command output as out of scope, and no test in the diff covers it.

After this change, gate output that had a credential redacted is dropped entirely from MCP responses, losing all diagnostics. Unrelated text that mentions "[redacted]" (titles, reasons, harness tool output that was already redacted) is also withheld. No test in the diff covers this change.

variants.detail: `json()` and the SSE `send` now pass every payload through `redactGateData`. The artifact endpoint also re-parses JSON artifacts and re-serializes them compactly, so it no longer serves the stored bytes. The prompt and report paths (`implementPrompt`, `reviewPrompt`, `renderReport`, `RunContext` constructor) do the same thing to whole input objects. Together this pushes the change to about 300 source lines against a stated budget of about 30, and the request explicitly asked for reda

variants.title: Scope well beyond the request: redaction of every HTTP/SSE response and of run state
variants.detail: The request asked for one redaction point in runGates plus the deploy gate, about 30 net source lines. The change adds about 115 net source lines. It round-trips every JSON response and SSE message through `redactGateData`, which strips VT sequences, redacts all strings and injects `confinementError` into any object shaped like `{ok, output}`. It also rewrites the whole RunState on every RunContext construction (context.ts:306) and re-redacts in each prompt builder and in renderReport. Each of these runs a full JSON serialize and parse on every call, and each changes data the request did not cover. The added code is hard to tell apart from the one place that actually matters.

variants.title: Every API response and SSE message is deep-cloned and rewritten
variants.detail: `json()` and `sse()` now pass all payloads, including run lists, stats, catalog and events, through `redactGateData`. That is a JSON round trip, a VT strip and a credential scan on every string, plus the `ok`/`output` object rewrite. It is unrequested scope, adds a per-message cost on hot SSE paths, and silently changes the shape of any unrelated object that happens to have `ok` and `output` fields.

variants.title: Artifact endpoint re-serializes JSON artifacts compactly and alters non-gate artifacts
variants.detail: `redactGateArtifact` runs `JSON.parse` and then `JSON.stringify` with no indent on every artifact that parses as JSON. Pretty-printed artifacts such as `gates-N.json`, `baseline-gates.json` and the review-shadow JSON are written with `JSON.stringify(x, null, 2)` and are now served on one line, which the UI shows as raw text. The replacer also adds a `confinementError` field to any object that has `ok` and `output` keys, and `stripVTControlCharacters` is applied to every artifact, including `diff.patch` and `spec.md`.

variants.title: Artifact endpoint re-serializes JSON artifacts and strips control sequences from patches
variants.detail: `redactGateArtifact` runs `JSON.parse` and then `JSON.stringify` with no indent on every artifact that parses as JSON. It also passes the data through `redactGateData`, which adds a `confinementError` field to every object that has `ok` and `output` keys. Artifacts written with `JSON.stringify(x, null, 2)` (gates-N.json, baseline-gates.json, review-shadow artifacts) are now served as one compact line with extra fields. Text artifacts such as diff.patch go through `stripVTControlCharacters`, so the served patch can differ from the stored one. The same VT stripping applies to the inline `patch` given to `reviewPrompt` through `redactGateData(input)`.

variants.title: Whole prompt inputs (including the patch under review) go through gate-output sanitization
variants.detail: `implementPrompt`, `reviewPrompt` and `verifyPrompt` now run their entire input through `redactGateData`, which applies `stripVTControlCharacters` and credential redaction to every string. That includes the request prompt, the spec, the implementer report and the inline `patch` of the change under review, not just the gate results. The request asked for redaction once, where `runGates` builds the result, so every consumer gets text that is already clean. Here the review model is shown a different diff from the one that will merge.

variants.title: reviewPrompt VT-strips the inline patch, so reviewers cannot see escape sequences that an external PR introduces
variants.detail: `input = redactGateData(input)` runs stripVTControlCharacters over every string in the review input. That includes `patch`, which is inlined for PR verification of external, untrusted changes. Raw ESC/CSI sequences added by the change, such as terminal-injection or concealment codes in source files, are silently removed from what the reviewer sees. The verify prompt and the artifact endpoint do the same.

variants.title: New `stdoutTruncated`/`stderrTruncated` result fields are unused
variants.detail: `ProcResult` gains per-stream truncation flags, and `hardening.test.ts` tests them, but nothing in `src` reads them. This is extra churn against a budget of about 30 lines.

variants.title: Unused per-stream truncation flags added to ProcResult
variants.detail: `stdoutTruncated` and `stderrTruncated` are computed and returned, but nothing in src reads them. Only the new tests in hardening.test.ts and proc.test.ts check them.

variants.title: confinementError is now always written and output is VT-stripped, which changes how an older release reads new results
variants.detail: The removed comment said confinementError was 'present only when set … so results stay readable by … older releases'. It is now always written, and `output` is now VT-stripped. An older release reads `!!confinementError || output.includes(marker)`. For output whose raw text was `Oper\x1b[0mation`, the new version records confinementError: false. After stripping, the stored output contains the full marker, so an older release reading the row would classify it as a confinement error. This only matters on rollback.

variants.title: Clean-filter tests never hit the key-enumeration race from #402

prompt:
## Decision
Triage moves to Codex Luna first, then Claude Haiku 5.5 (owner decision, 2026-10-07). Evidence on the 30 held-out triage cases, k=3: `claude/haiku-5.5@medium` passed 73.3% (Wilson 95% CI 63–81), with 0 of 84 risk under-calls, 10% flips and a 3.4 s p50 (<run-id>). The stored production baseline `codex/luna@medium` passed 71.1% (61–80), with 2 of 84 under-calls and 23% flips (<run-id>). Both are within noise. Haiku 5.5 is the fallback, not a replacement.

## Change
1. A built-in catalog model `claude/haiku-5.5` in `src/router/catalog.ts`: backend model `claude-haiku-5-5`, vendor anthropic, origin US, base origin US, tier 3, price $0.10 input / $0.50 output per million tokens with $0.01 cache reads, efforts low, medium and high, default medium. Its notes say that prompts over 100k tokens cost $0.50 / $2.50, and that its tokenizer counts about 30% more tokens than Haiku 4.5. `claude/haiku` (Haiku 4.5) stays unchanged.
2. The triage chain in `routing/policy.json` becomes `codex/luna@medium`, then `claude/haiku-5.5@medium`, then the existing fallbacks in their current order. Record the decision and the evidence above in `routing/overrides.json` and `routing/EVIDENCE.md`, following the existing entries (for example the 2026-10-04 Sonnet 5.5 decision).
3. Make sure regenerating the policy (`limitless eval policy --write`) keeps this order. If regeneration would reorder it, record it the way other owner decisions are kept.
4. This installation already has a runtime catalog entry with the id `claude/haiku-5.5` (added with `limitless catalog add`). Check what the daemon does when a runtime entry has the same id as a new built-in. Startup must not fail. Prefer the built-in and log that the runtime entry is redundant, or document `limitless catalog remove`. Don't silently merge the two.

## Tests
- The routing for a triage task resolves to `codex/luna@medium` first and `claude/haiku-5.5@medium` second, and falls back to Haiku 5.5 when the Codex provider is unavailable.
- The catalog entry validates and prices a call correctly.
- A runtime entry that duplicates a built-in id is handled as decided in step 4.

## Budget
About 40 net source lines, plus tests and the routing files.

## Out of scope
- Summarize, chat and implement-trivial routing (they keep `claude/haiku|codex/luna`).
- Changing `claude/haiku` or its backend model.
- Re-running any eval.

variants.detail: Startup skips the stored runtime model (continue) and keeps only the built-in in this.models. RuntimeCatalog.remove(id) calls editable(id), which finds the built-in (source undefined/'code') and throws '<id>: code and config models are read-only'. So `limitless catalog remove claude/haiku-5.5` cannot delete the stale runtime_models row; it persists indefinitely, the daemon warns on every start, and the warning gives no remediation. The request's alternative path (document `limitless catalog remove`) is therefore also not workable.
