head: 3de1eb39c117eeb619cbf33ff1baf6d20da0ac7f
prompt:
# limitless init and doctor: one idempotent setup command and a read-only diagnosis

## Why
Setting up Limitless on a new machine today takes a series of manual steps: provider config, secrets, the launchd service, tunnel and smoke checks. For a fresh install (M6, docs/PLAN.md), setup should be one command that is safe to re-run, plus a read-only command for diagnosis.

Depends on #35 (config-defined providers).

## What
1. **`limitless doctor`** is read-only and safe any time. Each check prints ok/warn/fail with the exact fix:
   - **git** is ≥ 2.40.
   - **`gh auth status`** passes and has repo access. For a GitHub organization, SSO authorization is checked by a read against a configured repository; on a 403 with `X-GitHub-SSO` it prints "sign in to your identity provider, then `gh auth refresh`".
   - **The claude and codex CLIs** are installed and logged in.
   - **python3** is present, for the sandbox probe.
   - **Every configured provider** has its `api_key_env` variable present (names only, never values) and answers its health check.
   - **The daemon** is up, and its version matches the installed one.
   - **The last smoke results** and **access problems recorded in the feed** are reported.

   It never changes anything. `--json` gives machine-readable output.
2. **`limitless init`** is idempotent and runs in order:
   1. The doctor checks; it stops on a failure, printing the fix.
   2. Provider detection: the CLI logins become `preset = "claude"` / `"codex"`, and local OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible servers are probed on common loopback ports and offered.
   3. It writes or updates `[[providers]]` and asks a few questions with defaults: the repositories to enable, the merge policy, and discreet mode.
   4. It starts the service and waits until healthy.
   5. It runs the live smoke checks.
   6. It offers to register the MCP server with Claude Code and Codex, asking before it changes their config.

   A re-run only fills gaps and shows what is already set. `--yes` accepts defaults and `--repo <owner/name>` can repeat, so an agent can run the whole setup non-interactively. `--json` gives a summary.
3. **Docs:** GUIDE "Getting started" becomes `limitless init`, with doctor for troubleshooting. Placeholders only.

## Tests (fakes for CLIs, gh, launchd and HTTP; no network)
- Each doctor check passes, warns and fails with the fix text.
- Secrets are never printed.
- init on an empty config, on a partial config, and as a second run that changes nothing.
- `--yes` with `--json`.
- An init that stops on a failed check leaves no partial config.

## Out of scope
Homebrew packaging (#38), the service label rename (#287), and changing provider semantics (#35).

Budget: ≤ 350 changed source lines plus tests. Gate: `bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun test`.

Never kill processes you did not start (no pkill or killall by name): other runs, deploys and the user share this machine.

Closes #288

gold.summary: Configuration errors and encoded feed diagnostics can disclose registered secrets.
A failure after configuration replacement leaves initialization partially applied.
Initialization rewrites unrelated configuration formatting without preserving a rollback copy.
Doctor omits health probes for implicit providers and presets lacking an explicit health URL.
The command fake permits mutating operations during read-only diagnosis.
The registration test does not exercise preservation of existing vendor settings.
Initialization does not collect the requested discreet-mode preference.

variants.title: Apply new configuration to an already healthy daemon
variants.detail: Init writes missing provider and merge settings but skips service installation whenever the original daemon check passed. The daemon loads configuration at startup and has no reload path, so init reports success while it continues using the old settings. Reproduction: `bun test "$TMPDIR/setup-review.test.ts"` failed with `Expected to contain: "install"; Received: ["write /fake/config/config.toml", "write /fake/home/smoke-last.json"]`.

variants.title: Apply changed config to an already-running daemon
variants.detail: The service step only checks the preflight daemon status. If init writes new providers or a merge policy while the daemon is healthy, it skips installation/restart. Factory loads these settings at startup, so setup reports success while the daemon retains its old configuration. Command `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review.ts" reload` printed providers.added=[claude,codex,local-1234], effects=[smoke,mcp], then failed: `AssertionError: new provider config must reach the already-running daemon`.

variants.title: Apply config changes to an already healthy daemon
variants.detail: Init writes new providers and merge settings but skips service startup whenever the preflight daemon SHA matches. Factory loads its catalog and configuration at construction, so the running daemon continues using the previous settings. The isolated command `bun "$TMPDIR/setup-review.ts"` produced `healthy daemon config update: {"effects":["write","write"],"service":"already set","merge":"pr"}`, confirming configuration writes without a service update.

variants.title: Smoke-test the effective configured providers
variants.detail: The production smoke adapter calls scripts/smoke.ts, which selects providers, endpoints and models from the static catalog. Newly detected local providers are never exercised, and configured endpoint overrides are ignored. Reproduction: `bun test "$TMPDIR/smoke-review.test.ts"` used fake harnesses and a zero execution budget to inspect scheduled checks; it listed only built-in provider rows and failed `Expected: true; Received: false` for inclusion of configured local-1234.

variants.title: Run smoke checks against the effective provider catalog
variants.detail: The production smoke adapter calls the existing smoke main, which uses hard-coded PROVIDERS/MODELS rather than the config catalog. Newly detected local providers and custom endpoints are never exercised; both native CLIs are always exercised even when doctor permits one to be missing. Command `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review.ts" smoke` enumerated checks with a zero budget and no network. It reported detected=[claude,codex,local-1234], but smoke names contained only built-in providers, then failed: `AssertionError: smoke must exercise the detected local provider`.

variants.title: Run smoke checks against the detected provider configuration
variants.detail: The production smoke adapter invokes a runner that imports the fixed PROVIDERS/MODELS catalogs and always schedules both native CLIs. It does not use the configured catalog or detected CLI availability. Newly detected local providers receive no live smoke check, while an absent CLI that doctor explicitly permits as a warning is still exercised. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/setup-review.ts"` with a zero smoke budget, preventing live calls, confirmed selection of both Claude and Codex plus the fixed backend list.

variants.title: Check access to newly selected repositories before writing
variants.detail: Doctor runs before repository selection and only reads repositories already in the original config. Fresh --repo arguments receive syntax validation but no access or SSO check before configuration is written. Reproduction: `bun test "$TMPDIR/setup-review.test.ts"` printed `GitHub commands: [["gh","auth","status"]]` and failed the assertion that `gh api repos/restricted/private` was called.

variants.title: Check requested repository access before writing config
variants.detail: Doctor runs before repositories supplied through --repo or prompts are considered, and only reads a repository already in config. Fresh setup therefore never verifies access or organization SSO for its requested repository. Command `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review.ts" repo`, with a fake repository API returning an SSO 403, printed `{"code":0,"ghReads":[],"effects":["smoke","mcp"]}` and failed: `AssertionError: init must reject a requested repository with denied SSO access`.

variants.title: Check requested repository access before persisting setup
variants.detail: Doctor runs before flags.repo or prompted repositories enter the configuration. Those repositories receive only syntax validation before being saved, so setup never checks their access or organization SSO authorization. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-setup.ts"` with private/no-access returned `"result":0,"repositoryReads":[]` and persisted that repository.

variants.title: Implement the requested discreet-mode setup choice
variants.detail: Discreet mode is replaced with a hardcoded skipped message. Init never asks for or persists the requested choice. Reproduction: `bun test "$TMPDIR/setup-review.test.ts"` printed questions for repositories, merge policy and MCP only, then failed the discreet-question assertion with `Expected: true; Received: false`.

variants.title: Implement the requested discreet-mode setup question
variants.detail: Discreet mode is unconditionally replaced with a 'not available yet (#37)' summary string. Init never asks the required question or persists a choice, including during interactive setup. The request does not exempt this step.

variants.title: Implement the requested discreet-mode setup choice
variants.detail: Discreet mode is represented only by a hard-coded skipped message. Init neither asks for the preference nor persists it, despite this being an explicit setup requirement. The interactive probe recorded only provider, repository, merge-policy and MCP questions; no discreet-mode question occurred.

variants.title: Check configured providers that lack an explicit health URL
variants.detail: Provider diagnosis only makes a health request when healthUrl exists. Supported presets such as OpenRouter have no healthUrl, so doctor reports only that their key is present and never checks whether the provider answers. Focused command `bun --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-setup.ts"` with an OpenRouter preset and invalid test token returned only `provider:openrouter:key` as ok; the recorded HTTP requests were exclusively `/api/health` and `/api/github/access`.

variants.title: Do not treat a preset alias as the native provider
variants.detail: Candidate deduplication treats e.preset === id as evidence that the native provider is already configured, even when the entry has a different explicit id. Provider semantics allow an entry such as id="work-claude", preset="claude" with endpoint overrides. That entry does not represent the detected native claude provider, but init skips adding the requested native preset.

# Run agents and gates can kill the user's processes: confine signals to the run

## Why
Run agents can signal any process the user owns. On 2026-10-03, implementers ran `pkill -f "bun test"` while investigating slow tests:
- run <run-id> (codex, workspace-write sandbox), at 09:56:02 and at 11:47:16;
- run <run-id>, at 11:16:58 and 11:21:26;
- older runs did the same, and one started eight `yes` busy loops to simulate load.

Each `pkill` killed every matching process on the machine, not only the agent's own:
- 09:56:02: the daemon's deploy gate (`bun test`) died at that exact second, and the deploy failed. That failure had been blamed on machine load.
- 11:47:16: a `land-pr.sh` check running in another checkout died at that second.
- The kills also cut short other runs' gates, so those runs repeated paid work.

Codex's `-s workspace-write` Seatbelt profile confines writes but not signals. The Claude edit mode has no sandbox yet (#233). At work, the same command would kill the user's own processes and other tools'.

## What
1. **Research first.** Can both CLIs be confined so that an agent and its children can signal only processes in their own run?
   - macOS Seatbelt `signal` targets: `self`, `pgrp`, `children`, `same-sandbox`.
   - Whether an outer `sandbox-exec` profile composes with Codex's own Seatbelt use and with the Claude CLI's sandbox (a nested `sandbox_init` may fail).
   - A process-group or session approach for gates.
   Record the findings in `docs/research/`.
2. **Enforce it where the platform allows.** Agents (edit and read-only modes) and gate commands can signal only their own run's processes, applied with the #233 sandbox work. Fail closed like #233: a run that cannot be confined fails with a clear reason.
3. **Cheap layers that don't depend on 2:**
   - Implement and fix prompts state: never signal processes the agent did not start; never `pkill` or `killall` by name; other runs and the user share this machine.
   - Add Claude edit-mode deny rules for `pkill`, `killall` and `kill -9 -1`, and Codex's equivalent if one exists. Pattern rules are bypassable, so they are a backstop, not the fix.
4. **Detect it.** The harness parsers flag tool calls that signal by name or by pid (`pkill`, `killall`, `kill`, `xargs kill`, `process.kill`) in the run's event log and report as a warning. Feed a `run.warning` item when one is seen.

## Acceptance checks
- A live smoke check per harness: an agent that runs `pkill -f <marker>` cannot kill a marker process started outside the run, and can kill one it started itself.
- A gate command cannot kill a marker process started outside the run.
- The detector flags the commands above in a captured fixture and ignores unrelated text.

## Out of scope
Network and read isolation, file-write confinement (#233), and resource limits (CPU or memory) on agents and gates.

Budget: research doc, then at most 250 changed source lines plus tests and smoke checks. Chain after #233 if both touch the sandbox profile code.

Never kill processes you did not start (no pkill or killall by name): other runs, deploys and the user share this machine.

Closes #293

The signal detector misses common command wrappers and flags harmless process queries.
The report layer queries event storage directly rather than through the Store interface.
Repeated confinement error wrapping obscures the underlying failure.

# Audit: only inert media binaries pass without Allow: binary

## Why
After #284, binary content passes the audit without `Allow: binary` when the path matches `BINARY_PATH` (`src/gates/audit.ts`). That list mixes two kinds of file:
- **inert media:** images, audio, video, fonts, PDF;
- **files that carry code or data a reviewer cannot see:** executables and libraries (`wasm`, `so`, `dll`, `dylib`, `exe`, `class`, `pyc`), archives and packages (`zip`, `jar`, `war`, `apk`, `whl`, `tar`, `gz`, `7z`, …), office documents (`docx`, `xlsx`, `pptx`, `odt`, macro-capable), and databases (`sqlite`, `db`).

Meanwhile, an edit to an unknown opaque binary such as `bun.lockb` already requires `Allow: binary`, because the diff cannot show what changed. Executables and archives are at least as opaque and more dangerous, yet they pass. Decision (Matt, 2026-10-03): only inert media pass without an allowance.

## What
1. Split `BINARY_PATH` into `INERT_MEDIA_PATH`:
   - images: png, jpg/jpeg, gif, bmp, ico, webp, avif, tif/tiff, heic, psd;
   - audio and video: mp3, mp4, m4a, mkv, mov, avi, webm, ogg, wav, flac, aac;
   - fonts: woff, woff2, ttf, otf, eot;
   - documents: pdf;
   - 3D models: glb, fbx, blend.

   Every other binary, new or edited, requires `Allow: binary`. That includes executables, archives, packages, office documents, databases, lockfiles and unknown types.
2. The `binary-content` finding names the file and says that `Allow: binary` in the request permits it.
3. **Low, same code (from the #298 review):** `headTextPaths` uses `afterText.raw`, which counts LFS pointers as text, so a new pointer under an existing LFS rule gets a spurious "new/moved files under rule" warning. Use `afterText.text`.

## Acceptance checks
- New and edited `.wasm`, `.so`, `.jar`, `.zip`, `.docx` and `.sqlite` files with binary content block without `Allow: binary`, and pass with it.
- New and edited `.png`, `.woff2`, `.mp4` and `.pdf` files pass.
- A new strict LFS pointer under an existing `filter=lfs` rule produces no warning.

## Out of scope
- LFS confinement on hosts with git-lfs installed (#233).
- Classification performance (#298).

Budget: ≤ 40 changed source lines plus tests.

Closes #300

# Audit: only inert media binaries pass without Allow: binary

## Why
After #284, binary content passes the audit without `Allow: binary` when the path matches `BINARY_PATH` (`src/gates/audit.ts`). That list mixes two kinds of file:
- **inert media:** images, audio, video, fonts, PDF;
- **files that carry code or data a reviewer cannot see:** executables and libraries (`wasm`, `so`, `dll`, `dylib`, `exe`, `class`, `pyc`), archives and packages (`zip`, `jar`, `war`, `apk`, `whl`, `tar`, `gz`, `7z`, …), office documents (`docx`, `xlsx`, `pptx`, `odt`, macro-capable), and databases (`sqlite`, `db`).

Meanwhile, an edit to an unknown opaque binary such as `bun.lockb` already requires `Allow: binary`, because the diff cannot show what changed. Executables and archives are at least as opaque and more dangerous, yet they pass. Decision (Matt, 2026-10-03): only inert media pass without an allowance.

## What
1. Split `BINARY_PATH` into `INERT_MEDIA_PATH`:
   - images: png, jpg/jpeg, gif, bmp, ico, webp, avif, tif/tiff, heic, psd;
   - audio and video: mp3, mp4, m4a, mkv, mov, avi, webm, ogg, wav, flac, aac;
   - fonts: woff, woff2, ttf, otf, eot;
   - documents: pdf;
   - 3D models: glb, fbx, blend.

   Every other binary, new or edited, requires `Allow: binary`. That includes executables, archives, packages, office documents, databases, lockfiles and unknown types.
2. The `binary-content` finding names the file and says that `Allow: binary` in the request permits it.
3. **Low, same code (from the #298 review):** `headTextPaths` uses `afterText.raw`, which counts LFS pointers as text, so a new pointer under an existing LFS rule gets a spurious "new/moved files under rule" warning. Use `afterText.text`.

## Acceptance checks
- New and edited `.wasm`, `.so`, `.jar`, `.zip`, `.docx` and `.sqlite` files with binary content block without `Allow: binary`, and pass with it.
- New and edited `.png`, `.woff2`, `.mp4` and `.pdf` files pass.
- A new strict LFS pointer under an existing `filter=lfs` rule produces no warning.

## Out of scope
- LFS confinement on hosts with git-lfs installed (#233).
- Classification performance (#298).

Budget: ≤ 40 changed source lines plus tests.

Closes #300

# Implement: a stuck implementer's background process makes cleanup fail the run

Seen 2026-10-04 on run <run-id> (#353). The Codex implementer started the full test suite in the background, writing to `node_modules/.ci-check-final.log`, then polled that log until the stuck detector stopped it ("repeated the same shell call 6 times"). The background test process kept running. The worktree cleanup that follows (`git … clean -ffdxq`) then failed with `warning: could not lstat node_modules/…` (files changing under it), and the whole run failed instead of moving to the next implement round.

Fix:
1. When an agent invocation ends (normally, stuck, or cancelled), kill its whole process tree before any worktree cleanup. Background children must not outlive the invocation.
2. Treat a cleanup failure after a stuck/failed implement round as a round failure (retry the round, or escalate), not a run failure; retry the clean once after the kill.

Acceptance (fake harness): an implementer that spawns a long-running background writer and then stalls is stopped; its child is gone before cleanup; the run proceeds to the next round. A `git clean` that fails once is retried.

Small: about 40 lines plus tests.

Tracking issue: #377.

gold.summary: Shutdown drops an already claimed descendant when its parent exits.
Holdout snapshot deletion proceeds despite unconfirmed descendant termination.
Production scratch directories are never registered as process ownership roots.
Replacing a descendant environment removes it from invocation discovery.

variants.title: Cwd and birth time incorrectly establish process ownership
variants.detail: Any hidden-environment orphan born after invocation start with a cwd under the worktree is treated as an invocation member, without evidence of ancestry. This kills unrelated processes sharing that directory. A standalone check launched an independent sibling launcher that orphaned a shell in the invocation cwd. Command `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501/review-unrelated-orphan.ts` returned `{"exitCode":0,"unrelatedOrphanAliveAfterReturn":false}`.

variants.title: Birth time and working directory do not prove process ownership
variants.detail: The orphan fallback selects any hidden-environment process born during the invocation whose cwd is under a supplied root, even without a matching marker, session, group, or ancestor. stopMarkedProcesses then signals it. Another concurrent command or user process can satisfy these conditions. Exact probe command: bun -e 'import {hiddenDarwinProcessMember as member} from "./src/util/processes-darwin.ts"; console.log({unrelatedOrphanSelected:member(42,new Map([[42,1]]),new Set(),100,[process.cwd()],()=>101,()=>({path:process.cwd()}))});'. Output: { unrelatedOrphanSelected: true }.

variants.title: Directory-based orphan detection selects unrelated processes
variants.detail: Birth time, orphan status, and a shared working directory do not establish invocation ownership. This fallback selects unrelated platform processes launched during the invocation, and stopMarkedProcesses then signals them. A standalone reproduction launched an unmarked orphan shell independently of the invocation and scanned with an unrelated marker. Command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501/review-orphan.ts. variants.detail: The second checkoutCommitted call omits retryClean even when implementerIssue is set. If this clean fails, it throws CommandError rather than WorktreeCleanError, so the new recovery handler rethrows it and fails the run. A standalone probe of this call's default behavior, `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501/review-clean-retry.ts`, produced `{"errorType":"CommandError","cleanAttempts":1}` for a clean that would succeed on its second attempt.

variants.detail: Session/group membership is accepted only when the environment is hidden. # Verify: confined verifiers can't bind sockets, so tests with local servers block verification

Seen 2026-10-05 on review round 2 for #367 (run <run-id>). Implement and gates passed. The verify stage then ended the run as needs_human ("verification blocked by the environment"), because every CLI test that starts an ephemeral local server failed with `EADDRINUSE` inside the verifier's sandbox. The round's commit was never delivered, although gates had passed those same tests.

Gates (confined) can run these tests, but the confined reader the verifier uses cannot bind or listen on loopback.

Fix options:
1. Allow loopback bind/listen (127.0.0.1 / ::1, ephemeral ports only) in the verifier's read-only profile, as the gate profile does. No outbound network.
2. Or let the verifier cite the gates' results for tests it cannot run itself, rather than blocking.

Acceptance: a fake verify that runs a test binding `127.0.0.1:0` succeeds in the reader profile, and outbound connections stay denied.

Related: #369 (confinement profiles).

Tracking issue: #383.

gold.summary: The reader loopback policy cannot match the intended socket access.
An allow-default reader policy weakens the established confinement boundary.

variants.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for long verification commands
variants.detail: Bun.serve defaults to a 10-second connection idle timeout. This endpoint uses JSON responses and awaits the entire subprocess result before returning any bytes, so verification commands exceeding that interval lose their MCP connection even when the subprocess produces output. The request signal is included in the subprocess cancellation signal, so disconnecting can also terminate the test. Increasing the CLI tool timeout does not change this server timeout.

variants.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for long-running commands
variants.detail: Bun.serve defaults to a 10-second idle timeout. This bridge buffers command output and sends its JSON response only after executeReaderCommand finishes, so commands taking longer than that can lose their HTTP connection despite the much larger configured command and MCP timeouts. The request signal also participates in command cancellation, so the disconnect can terminate verification.

variants.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for long verification commands
variants.detail: Bun.serve retains its default 10-second idle timeout. The MCP transport uses enableJsonResponse, so no response bytes are sent while executeReaderCommand runs. Commands lasting beyond that timeout can lose their HTTP connection, which also aborts the subprocess through req.signal. Increasing MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT or tool_timeout_sec does not change this server timeout.

variants.title: Preserve installed Rust toolchain discovery when replacing HOME
variants.detail: Reader commands replace HOME with empty scratch without preserving RUSTUP_HOME. Standard rustup installations consequently lose their default compiler, although gates explicitly preserve RUSTUP_HOME in runConfined. Reproduced with `env HOME="$TMPDIR" rustup show active-toolchain`, which outputs `error: no active toolchain`. Adding `RUSTUP_HOME="$HOME/.rustup"` returns `stable-aarch64-apple-darwin (default)`.

variants.title: Restrict loopback binding to ephemeral ports
variants.detail: The wildcard network-bind rule permits binding any loopback TCP port. Restrictions on network-inbound prevent listening on service ports, but binding alone reserves a port and can prevent other local processes from using it. This violates the requested ephemeral-only restriction. The new test combines bind and listen, so a denial at listen hides the successful prohibited bind.

prompt:
# Verify: confined verifiers can't bind sockets, so tests with local servers block verification

Seen 2026-10-05 on review round 2 for #367 (run <run-id>). Implement and gates passed. The verify stage then ended the run as needs_human ("verification blocked by the environment"), because every CLI test that starts an ephemeral local server failed with `EADDRINUSE` inside the verifier's sandbox. The round's commit was never delivered, although gates had passed those same tests.

Gates (confined) can run these tests, but the confined reader the verifier uses cannot bind or listen on loopback.

Fix options:
1. Allow loopback bind/listen (127.0.0.1 / ::1, ephemeral ports only) in the verifier's read-only profile, as the gate profile does. No outbound network.
2. Or let the verifier cite the gates' results for tests it cannot run itself, rather than blocking.

Acceptance: a fake verify that runs a test binding `127.0.0.1:0` succeeds in the reader profile, and outbound connections stay denied.

Related: #369 (confinement profiles).

Tracking issue: #383.

gold.summary: A single extracted test command is treated as proof of a multi-step criterion.

variants.title: Require positive test execution evidence for targeted commands
variants.detail: The exact-file branch accepts a successful process whenever its output lacks failure or skip markers, even with no passing tests. Confirmed that Bun exits 0 and emits only its version and file header when a test module calls process.exit(0). Those actual output bytes are accepted as coverage. Targeted command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-AAmrsP/claude-501/review-gate-evidence.ts zero`. Output: `expected blocked; actual met`, followed by `error: Unverified criterion was marked met`.

variants.title: Require positive coverage for every explicitly requested file
variants.detail: The exact-command shortcut accepts matching file arguments without checking that each file ran. Bun treats these arguments as filters and exits successfully when one matches and another is missing. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/limitless-383-review.test.ts". The missing-file regression printed `gate exit: 0 ran: Ran 1 test across 1 file.` and failed with `Expected: "blocked", Received: "met"`.

variants.title: The targeted-command shortcut ignores evidence that the requested file never passed
variants.detail:
When selected and requested arguments match, the shortcut returns true without checking passedFiles—even when retained coverage explicitly contains only another file. Bun treats an argument without ./ as a substring filter. In a temporary fixture containing an empty test/loopback.test.ts and a passing nested/test/loopback.test.ts, the exact command `bun test test/loopback.test.ts` exited 0 with output: `test/loopback.test.ts:

nested/test/loopback.test.ts:
(pass) unrelated [0.03ms]

 1 pass
 0 fail
 1 expect() calls
Ran 1 test across 2 files.` Applying that result produced `SUBSTITUTED STATUS: met` and failed the assertion `ASSERTION FAILED: required file ran zero tests; only nested/

variants.title: Partial command parsing can approve tests that never ran
variants.detail: The regex extracts only a command prefix and silently discards unsupported syntax or remaining instructions. For `bun test "test/loopback.test.ts"`, it extracts bare `bun test`, allowing any passing file to satisfy the criterion. It also ignores additional verification steps after a newline. Targeted command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/verifier-evidence-review.test.ts"`. Both cases failed with `Expected: "blocked"; Received: "met"` (0 pass, 2 fail).

variants.title: Partial test coverage incorrectly satisfies an entire blocked criterion
variants.detail: The matcher extracts a Bun command from verification instructions and ignores additional checks. applyGateEvidence then marks the entire criterion met without checking whether the blocked operation was covered. Reproduction command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-EZtPeE/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-EZtPeE/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-EZtPeE/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-EZtPeE/claude-501/review-gate-coverage.ts`. Output: `AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: 'met' !== 'blocked'`.

variants.title: Check tested working-tree bytes before recording commit provenance
variants.detail: Evidence eligibility checks only HEAD, after discardChanges has erased gate modifications. Setup commands and earlier checks can modify tracked source or tests without changing HEAD. Subsequent tests then pass against those modified bytes, but the new evidence attributes that pass to the original commit and can override a blocked independent verification.

variants.title: Interrupted gate completion permanently disables evidence on resume
variants.detail: RunContext.stage persists completedChecks and gateEvidence before marking the gate stage succeeded. A crash between those writes leaves cached successful checks referencing a running stage, which scheduler recovery marks cancelled. On resume, the gates cache bypasses execution, but this new status check rejects its evidence. Neither verification attempt repairs or reruns the gates, so an otherwise passing run ends as environment-blocked.

head: f32796e092a23fd6d1f16142660c56ffcda35f7b
prompt:
Closes #376. Land/delivery pushes must not run commands named by repository config.

## Why
After PR code has run (unconfined in `scripts/land-pr.sh`'s `bun run check`), the land push uses hardened settings (`safe_git`: no hooks, filters, fsmonitor, commit-graph, bitmaps), but repository-level git config can still make the push execute a command: `remote.<name>.receivepack` (probed: it ran after the final scan), and by the same mechanism `remote.<name>.pushurl` pointing at an `ext::` URL, `core.sshCommand`, `credential.helper` (including URL-scoped `credential.<url>.helper`), `gpg.program`, and keys pulled in through `include.path`/`includeIf`. None can change what is pushed (the pack is built with hardened settings and the SHA is pinned); this is defence in depth for the window after the final scan.

## What
Apply one rule to every factory push: `scripts/land-pr.sh`'s final push, the land queue's push (src/land/), and the delivery push (src/git/): **repository-level config is untrusted for the push; global and system config are trusted.**
- Push to an explicit URL (the trusted remote URL the factory already knows, not one read from repository config), so `remote.<name>.*` (receivepack, pushurl, uploadpack) is never consulted; and pass `-c protocol.ext.allow=never`.
- Command-running keys: reset them for the push and re-add only the values from trusted scopes. For example read `git config --global --get-all credential.helper` (and `--system`) and pass `-c credential.helper=` followed by `-c credential.helper=<each trusted value>`; for `core.sshCommand` use the global/system value if set, else `ssh`; never let a repository-scoped or included value apply. Credentials must keep working exactly as today (the owner's pushes use their existing global helper or SSH setup); if the trusted-scope lookup itself could be influenced by the repository, explain why it can't (e.g. `--global` reads only the global file).
- URL-scoped keys (`credential.<url>.helper`, `url.<base>.insteadOf`/`pushInsteadOf`) from repository config must not apply either: either neutralise them explicitly or run the push with repository config excluded (if you choose an approach such as pushing from a separate trusted repository/bare cache, show that it pushes exactly the pinned SHA and keeps the hardening).
- Keep `safe_git` hardening and the exact-SHA pin.

## Tests (no network, no real gh; read test/AGENTS.md)
For each push path, plant in the checkout's repository config: `remote.origin.receivepack`, `remote.origin.pushurl=ext::…`, `core.sshCommand`, `credential.helper`, `credential.<url>.helper`, `url.<x>.insteadOf`, `gpg.program`, and an `include.path` file carrying one of them; each pointing at a script that would create a marker file. Push to a local bare remote (file URL) and assert: no marker file exists, the remote received exactly the pinned SHA, and a trusted GLOBAL `credential.helper` (set via GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL in the test) is still invoked when the transport needs credentials (use a local HTTP-free approach if needed, e.g. assert the effective `-c` arguments passed, plus one end-to-end file-URL push). Note CI runners have git-lfs filters configured outside the test's global file; don't assert exact full argv.

Budget: about 80 changed source lines plus tests. Out of scope: confining land-pr.sh's `bun run check` itself.

gold.summary: An inherited Git configuration selector redirects trusted SSH lookup into the checkout.
Trusted remote-dependent credential and SSH settings no longer apply during push.
Manual landing publishes a fork branch to the upstream repository.
Forcing HTTPS during manual push bypasses working SSH authentication.

variants.title: Preserve reftable storage when constructing the isolated repository
variants.detail: The isolated repository copies only objects, refs and packed-refs, then declares repository format 0. It omits reftable storage and `extensions.refStorage`, so source references cannot resolve in a reftable repository. In a fixture created with `git init --ref-format=reftable`, `bash scripts/push-git.sh git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push --no-follow-tags "$url" HEAD:refs/heads/using-head` returned 1 with `error: src refspec HEAD does not match any`; the same Git push without the wrapper succeeded. Normal delivery still calls pushBranch with `HEAD` in src/pipeline/engine.ts.

variants.title: Preserve the repository's reference storage format
variants.detail: The isolated directory preserves objects and file-based refs but omits reftable storage and extensions.refStorage. Reproduced in a repository initialized with `git init --ref-format=reftable`: a normal file-URL push of `HEAD:refs/heads/default-baseline` succeeded, while the equivalent push through this helper exited 1 with `error: src refspec HEAD does not match any`. pushBranch accepts HEAD by default, and the pipeline also explicitly passes HEAD on a delivery path.

variants.title: Reconstructed administration loses reftable references
variants.detail: The temporary common directory preserves only files-based refs and object-format metadata. It omits extensions.refStorage and reftable storage. A local repository initialized with `git init --ref-format=reftable` successfully pushed an explicit SHA through the wrapper, but the equivalent wrapper push using `HEAD:refs/heads/default` exited 1 with `error: src refspec HEAD does not match any`. Production delivery still passes HEAD in several paths.

variants.title: The SSH default overrides trusted GIT_SSH
variants.detail: When core.sshCommand is unset, injecting core.sshCommand=ssh overrides Git's existing GIT_SSH environment setting. A network-free probe used GIT_SSH to run a local receive-pack: `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push "$destination" "$sha:refs/heads/before"` succeeded, while `bash scripts/push-git.sh git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push "$destination" "$sha:refs/heads/after"` exited 128 with `fatal: Could not read from remote repository.` The invocation markers were `trusted` followed by `fallback`, proving the wrapper bypassed GIT_SSH.

prompt:
Loop detection: a repeated tool call whose result changed is progress, not a loop.

## Why
`LoopDetector` (src/harness/types.ts) stops an agent when the same tool call (name + input) appears 6 times in a 12-call window. It never looks at results. Implementers commonly start the full test suite in the background and poll its log with one identical command (e.g. `tail -n 6 <log>; rg -c '^\(pass\)' <log>`) while the count grows. Three runs on 2026-10-07 (<run-id>, <run-id>, <run-id>) were each ended as "stuck: repeated the same shell call 6 times" while polling a progressing test run; each lost the rest of its implementation round and the implementer never saw its own test results.

## What
- Feed tool results to the detector in both harnesses (src/harness/codex.ts and src/harness/claude.ts already parse tool calls and their results; match a result to its call by the call id the CLIs provide).
- An identical call counts toward the loop only if its result is identical (compare a hash of the result text, after the output truncation the parsers already apply) to the result of the previous identical call. When the result differs, that call does not count, and earlier occurrences of the same key are dropped from the window, so a poll whose output keeps changing never trips the detector. A call whose result never arrives (still running, or the session ends) counts as today.
- Keep the tool-call budget (`exceeded tool-call budget`) unchanged; it still bounds polling.
- The stop reason stays the same text when the detector does trip.

Each new test fails with the change reverted.

prompt:
## Problem
This repository's test suite is the main cost of every factory run here (M5.1). It was measured on 2026-10-08 on a quiet machine (main at 12303dd, Bun 1.4.2, 18 cores).
- **Serial `bun test`:** 1,592 s wall (26.5 min); 770 s user and 1,103 s system CPU. Files run strictly one after another (the per-file times sum to the wall time).
- **One file is half the suite.** `test/pipeline.test.ts` takes 751 s (47%, 383 tests, about 2 s each with real git and gates). The five largest files are 83%: pipeline 751 s, failure-injection 157 s, land-pr 156 s, evals-implement-runner 146 s, git-integrity 113 s. 93 of 126 files take under 1 s.
- **`bun test --parallel=6`:** 888 s wall (1.8× faster); 862 s user, 1,558 s system. The floor is `test/pipeline.test.ts`, because Bun parallelizes by file.
- **One test failed under parallel load:** "pipeline (fake agents, real git + gates) > panel mode: deep roster plus base lenses, local=%s". The same test failed once in Linux CI on 2026-10-08 (#419) and passed on rerun, so it is flaky under load generally.

Bun 1.4.2 supports `--parallel=N` (file-level worker processes; implies `--isolate`), `--timings` (slowest files first) and `--shard`.

## Change
1. **Run test files in parallel** wherever this repository runs its full suite: the `test` script used by `bun run check`, the `[gates]` test command in `.limitless.toml`, the CI workflow, and the deploy gate's test command (`GATES` in `src/cli/service.ts`). Pick the worker count by measurement on a quiet machine (for example 4, 6 and 8; report all three). Several factory gates can run at once on one machine, so prefer a moderate fixed default over "all cores", and make it overridable with one environment variable.
2. **Split `test/pipeline.test.ts`** into several files grouped by topic, so that no file takes more than about 2 minutes serially. Move shared setup and helpers into a support module. Move every test unchanged: no deletions, no weakened assertions, no skipped tests. Check that the total test count before and after is equal.
3. **Fix the flaky panel-mode test's cause** (likely a wait or timeout that doesn't hold under CPU contention), so it passes reliably under `--parallel` and in CI. Don't just raise its timeout without understanding why it fails.
4. **Update test/AGENTS.md.** Process-isolated parallel files (`--parallel`) are allowed. Blanket in-process concurrency (`--concurrent`, shared globals such as process.env, spies, timers and gate slots) still isn't. New test files must be safe to run in parallel.

## Measure (in the PR description)
Wall time and user/system CPU, serial against parallel, on a quiet machine, with the per-file top 10 after the split. Run the full suite in parallel at least three times with zero failures.

## Out of scope
- Making individual tests cheaper (fewer subprocesses per pipeline test). That comes next, measured separately.
- Factory changes (gate scheduling, baselines, concurrency across runs).
- Deleting or skipping tests.

## Budget
Mostly moving tests between files; source changes of about 20 lines (scripts, config, the deploy gate command).

prompt:
Fixes #423.

## Decision (2026-10-09)
PR #429 moved holdout redaction from write time to output time: it stored verifier diagnostics in full and redacted each agent- and GitHub-facing output. Its reviews kept finding outputs without the guard (provider records, restored state, clipped tool-call previews, MCP error responses, agent-requested SSE and artifact endpoints, the review-round PR section, several prompt families), so every new output path would need to remember it. #429 is closed. This is the design to use instead.

## Problem
Main redacts a verify or holdout invocation's output when it is written (`redactHoldout` in `src/pipeline/context.ts`, and the run error detail in `src/pipeline/engine.ts`). Everything an agent or GitHub can see is therefore holdout-safe by construction, but the owner loses the same diagnostics: for example #422's verify run errors and the providers' structured 400 responses were scrubbed, which hid why verification failed.

## Change
1. **Keep main's write-time redaction unchanged.** Every stored record that agents, prompts, MCP, REST, SSE, the digest or GitHub can read stays exactly as main writes it today.
2. **Also keep an owner-only copy of the raw text** wherever write-time redaction changed something: the verify and holdout invocations' raw error, result text and event messages, and the raw detail behind the redacted run error. Store it only where agents can't read it:
   - never returned by any MCP tool, prompt, digest, feed item or GitHub text;
   - never served by the HTTP/SSE API to a request that isn't the owner (check how `src/server/http.ts` and `src/server/auth.ts` decide that, including local unauthenticated requests; if the API can't tell, don't serve it over HTTP at all);
   - not in a path an agent sandbox can read (check the editor and reader read rules: `privateReadRoots`, `denyRead`, the factory home).
   A new table or a file under the run's private directory both work; add any table in a new additive migration.
3. **Show it to the owner:** `limitless show <run>` and `limitless logs <run>` print the owner diagnostics next to the redacted records, clearly marked, and the owner UI may show them if it can do so under the same rule.
4. Credential redaction still applies to the owner copy (`redactCredentials`).

## Tests
- A verify invocation whose error, result and events contain authored holdout text and runtime literals: every agent-, prompt- and GitHub-facing path shows exactly what main shows today, and `limitless show`/`logs` show the raw text.
- The owner copy is not reachable through any MCP tool on either transport, nor through the REST/SSE API without owner authorization.
- A run that never redacted anything stores no owner copy.
- A run created before the change still displays and resumes (no owner copy, no error).

## Budget
About 150 source lines plus tests, mostly additive.

## Out of scope
- Changing what agents, prompts or GitHub receive.
- Redacting more than main does today.

head: 261559da0ec2376d0c2614ce30205f81e43e94bd
prompt:
## What happens
Delivery pushes the worktree's current HEAD (`const head = sha ?? (await headSha(cwd))` in `deliver`, `src/pipeline/engine.ts`). It doesn't check that this commit is the one the gates, audit and review checked. Review records `ctx.state.reviewedSha`, but only the verify-change flow compares it with HEAD.

A run that stops between review and delivery and resumes with a different HEAD therefore pushes a commit nothing checked.

Reproduced on main (2026-10-10) with the `test/review-rounds.test.ts` harness:
1. A review round is killed by the fault plan `{ "stage:deliver:before": { action: "kill" } }`.
2. The round's worktree commit is amended (`fix.txt` changed, same parent).
3. The daemon restarts.

The round ends `succeeded` and the PR branch holds the amended commit `91cda74`, not the reviewed `18e60a1`.

Only the factory writes a run's git admin directory, so this is a gap in "act on the exact commit you checked" (AGENTS.md), not a known exploit. #458's review found it while checking conflict rounds, which deliver through the same code.

## Change
- Before any push (review-round delivery, existing-branch delivery and new-PR delivery), require HEAD to equal the commit recorded by the last passing gates and review for this round.
- If it differs, refuse without pushing and end the run needs_human with a reason naming both SHAs.
- The check runs on the resume path as well as the first attempt, through one shared helper.

## Tests (fake agents, local bare repository, fault plan; no network)
- The scenario above pushes nothing and ends needs_human. It fails on main.
- An ordinary resume with HEAD unchanged still delivers once.
- The same check holds for a new-PR delivery and an existing-branch delivery.

## Budget
About 30 changed source lines plus tests.

## Out of scope
- Re-running gates or review automatically after a mismatch.
- Conflict rounds' own delivery checks (#458).

gold.summary: A resumed delivery whose base advanced again after a completed factory merge is refused, because the check requires the second merge's first parent to be the reviewed commit instead of the earlier factory merge.

variants.title: Handle interrupted gate completion before rejecting cached evidence
variants.detail: RunContext.stage persists completedChecks.values.gates before calling finishStage(..., "succeeded"). If the daemon stops between those writes, restart reuses the cached gate result without executing or completing that stage. Its recorded status remains non-succeeded, so this new guard refuses delivery even though HEAD is unchanged and subsequent audit, review and verification pass. This introduces a needs_human outcome for an ordinary resumable run.

variants.title: Errors before the guard can still push through draft fallback
variants.detail: The first guard runs after the resumed-delivery GitHub lookup. If that lookup throws, executeScopedRun enters deliverVerifiedDraft because the error is not DeliveryHeadError. That function pushes lastVerifiedSha without calling the shared guard. Thus an amended HEAD can still cause a push and draft creation rather than the required refusal naming both SHAs. The fallback suppression only covers mismatches that execution actually reaches.

variants.title: Pending-merge exception accepts unreviewed amendments
variants.detail: validateMerge checks only the two parent SHAs, so amending a pending factory merge with arbitrary file changes still satisfies this exception. On resume, mergeForDelivery accepts that amended merge, runs post-merge gates, and records it as the delivery head without auditing or reviewing the amendment. The requested refusal therefore remains bypassable. An isolated probe executing the actual helper and validator against real git failed: `bun "$TMPDIR/delivery-head-probe.ts"` printed `refused: false` and `AssertionError: An amended pending merge must be refused before delivery`.

variants.title: Do not authorize a changed merge commit from its parents alone
variants.detail: When pendingRebaseSha is set, this exception accepts any HEAD with the expected two parents. validateMerge checks ancestry, not the commit's tree or an exact recorded SHA. Amending a pending clean merge preserves those parents, so resume accepts the unreviewed amendment, reruns post-merge gates, and pushes it without review or audit. A temporary Git fixture invoking validateMerge after such an amendment printed: `validateMerge accepted amended, unreviewed HEAD: ce8e0282e9e7af6360d1efdead30a1c22a0656d6`.

head: 133e274c8e0471f016e179b44ab9a064db6d4b8b
prompt:
# Implement: a stuck implementer's background process makes cleanup fail the run

Seen 2026-10-04 on run <run-id> (#353). The Codex implementer started the full test suite in the background, writing to `node_modules/.ci-check-final.log`, then polled that log until the stuck detector stopped it ("repeated the same shell call 6 times"). The background test process kept running. The worktree cleanup that follows (`git … clean -ffdxq`) then failed with `warning: could not lstat node_modules/…` (files changing under it), and the whole run failed instead of moving to the next implement round.

Fix:
1. When an agent invocation ends (normally, stuck, or cancelled), kill its whole process tree before any worktree cleanup. Background children must not outlive the invocation.
2. Treat a cleanup failure after a stuck/failed implement round as a round failure (retry the round, or escalate), not a run failure; retry the clean once after the kill.

Acceptance (fake harness): an implementer that spawns a long-running background writer and then stalls is stopped; its child is gone before cleanup; the run proceeds to the next round. A `git clean` that fails once is retried.

Small: about 40 lines plus tests.

Tracking issue: #377.

gold.summary: Detached descendants survive invocation cleanup and keep modifying the worktree.
Process cleanup returns while owned descendants are still alive.
Discarding changes replaces the cleanup error that should trigger round recovery.

variants.title: Cleanup failures from the finally block still fail the run
variants.detail: The handler recognizes only WorktreeCleanError from the initial checkoutCommitted call. The unconditional discardChanges in the gates' finally block uses git clean -fdq without retry and throws an ordinary CommandError. That bypasses this handler even after a stuck implementer. Its exception can also replace an initial WorktreeCleanError, defeating the new recovery path.

prompt:
Found by the new-agent test (#473): MCP tool outputs too large for an agent to read.

## What happened
- `limitless_list_runs` with no arguments returned 99 KB (every run ever), over the client's limit. With `limit: 3` it worked.
- `limitless_get_run` output was large enough that the agent avoided it ("Those outputs are big").
- `list_runs` showed `merged: true` while `mergedBy` and `mergedAt` were still null; `limitless_status` was right.

## Change
1. `limitless_list_runs` defaults to a small limit, newest first, with `repo` and `status` filters, and says when more remain.
2. `limitless_get_run` returns a compact summary by default (state, stage, PR, head SHA, delivered rounds, land entry, last error), with an option for full detail.
3. The merge fields are consistent: `mergedAt` and `mergedBy` are set when `merged` is, or omitted until known.

Additive changes only. Old fields stay available through the full-detail option.

## Tests
- Default sizes stay under a byte budget with many runs.
- The filters work.
- `merged` and its fields agree.
